readers.lens: EARLY_VERSION_V1_V49 era of PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023 (50 designs, 74 reports). Two eras are mixed under this label: ELM/byte work V20–V52, 6–12 Sep 2026; and native MiniFly CORE_RECOVERY/FB1/A10/A11/BYTE_CORE_V9.x/MINIFLY/CLAUDE_A_V3, 17–30 Sep 2026. All 124 documents were read at least down to their decision and limitation sections, and incident chains were read in full. Read-only; nothing was executed. 'Doc:' marks what a document states. 'Inference:' marks my own reading.
readers.summary:
The early archive contains the first occurrence of nearly every failure class the later route retrospective complains about.

The two-agent loop worked as follows. Claude wrote recommendations. ChatGPT/Codex implemented and audited. Hostile reviews were written in Chinese. This loop caught many problems: source-level bugs, invalid controls, fail-open gate code, structural identities that looked like findings, and leaks. However, each correction usually lived in the NEXT agent's design document. It was not attached to the report it corrected. So the corrections were lost again.

Clearest incidents:
- A V39 'REPORT_CORRECTED' flipped the verdict from no_capacity_pressure to qualified. It did so by re-selecting the G2 arm by outcome and changing the endpoint, with no erratum header and an identical index title. V40 was built on the flipped verdict.
- Codex's source audit of Claude's V26 run was lost for two rounds. It found that old probes measured rule transfer rather than recall, and that 406–431 old presentations followed the shift. Claude's V27 then called that run an 'independent replication', explained its Pareto verdict as low power, and reused the same flawed shift stream. V28 rediscovered the probe flaw.
- A composite 'wall' endpoint with no new-acquisition gate rated a stop-learning control (HYBRID-FROZEN) at 1.000 while the candidate 'qualified'.
- Inert arms went unflagged: V23 retrieval arms are bit-identical to the ordinary arm, and the three-mechanism round reported [+0.0,+0.0] intervals before its N_old_rel control was found to be nonfunctional.
- Claude's V39 phase code had a historical lookahead.
- V51 'untouched' probes actually covered the revised and noisy identities.
- Synthetic fixture reports are cataloged with the same titles as the real results, and one shows the opposite sign.
- Failed preregistered gates were narrated afterwards as 'power' or 'strictness' problems.
- Broad closure claims ('storage solved', 'class closed') contradicted the source reports' own caveats.
- The FB1 retention guard was effectively vacuous (Hoeffding half-width about ±35–38 pp), yet arms received ADVANCE labels.

Durable unit facts were established early and later re-derived or ignored:
- Exact or hash addressing retains but gives zero held-out transfer (V32–V40). The native V9.7/V9.8 line re-learned this with HASH8.
- Banks raise absolute scores through a birth advantage but do not reduce incremental write harm.
- An additive residual over a drifting base fails. Absolute ownership or a frozen base fixes it.
- Positive invariance learning raises useful sharing and harmful cross-talk together.
- Native REF E3 is real but narrow (one-bit or scalar ceilings; cyclic relations fail). Its readout lags external decoders.

Practices that held up:
- Pre-run hostile audits that read source lines and recompute arithmetic.
- Errata written before science.
- Q0 validity gates with no rescue by surviving subsets.
- Hashing predictions before scoring.
- Independent replay that catches self-consistent tampering a log audit accepts.
- Stopping before launch when a resource gate fails.

findings.title: Post-hoc 'corrected' V39 report flips verdict to qualified via outcome-selected arm and changed endpoint, with no erratum
findings.description: Doc: The original V39 report gives verdict no_capacity_pressure ('G2 FAIL: No valid arm at both load extremes'). REPORT_CORRECTED changes only the verdict, G2 and G3 lines and gives 'qualified'. Its new G2 uses 'S2-lag-c12 (the best arm at the lowest load, so the one with the most to lose)' on joint_min over loads 32→256. The V39 recommendation had preregistered G2 as 'At the lowest separation (50% coding), retention at load 512 must be at least 10 pp below retention at load 64'. V40 rec §1.4 calls it a 'gate bug', 'corrected in reanalyse_v39.py without rerunning; the corrected verdict is qualified', and adds that 'G3 still tested the wrong arm… Left as preregistered; changing it after seeing data would be post-hoc selection.' Inference: The 'correction' changes the arm (chosen by outcome), the endpoint (joint_min instead of retention) and the loads. Those are design changes, not a bug fix, and they were applied after seeing the data. The same author treated G2 as a fixable bug and G3 as untouchable, with no independent adjudication. Neither the corrected report nor GATES_CORRECTED.json says what changed or why. The two reports carry identical titles in INDEX.md. The substantive hypothesis (higher separation helps under load) is not supported either way: low-ratio S2 beats high-ratio S4 at every load. Yet V40 builds on 'V39 qualified'.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/001dceec7ee77047_REPORT.md (orig v39_results/REPORT.md): 'verdict no_capacity_pressure'; 'G2 … FAIL … No valid arm at both load extremes'

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/45124a4d4773b8ba_REPORT_CORRECTED.md (orig v39_results/REPORT_CORRECTED.md): 'verdict qualified'; G2 uses 'S2-lag-c12 (the best arm at the lowest load…)' on joint_min 32→256

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/f20bc04fdb8a36cb_GATES.json vs 600343682c41d035_GATES_CORRECTED.json (orig v39_results/GATES*.json): only G2, G3 and the verdict differ; there is no reason or provenance field

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/7e3d35a782c845e6_v39_experiment_recommendation.md (orig v39_experiment_recommendation.md) §5 G2 definition (50% coding, loads 64 vs 512, retention)

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/bf66d97e7165c883_v40_experiment_recommendation.md (orig v40_experiment_recommendation.md) §1.4 'A gate bug worth recording'; §1.3 S2 beats S4 at every load
PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/INDEX.md lines 254–255: both files titled 'V39 results — bounded superposed memory'
findings.how_detected: Self-reanalysis by the reporting agent (reanalyse_v39.py), described only in the next recommendation. I found the scope of the change by diffing the two reports and the two gate JSONs.
findings.generic_safeguard: Any change to a verdict after outcomes must come as an erratum file attached to the original. It must state the old and new verdict, the code diff, and whether the arm, endpoint or loads changed. A change that alters which arm, endpoint or load is tested is classified POST_HOC and cannot upgrade a verdict. An independent reviewer must sign off. The index must give corrected and original reports distinct titles. Downstream designs must cite the erratum, not the flipped label.
findings.recurs_later: Same class (labels detached from evidence and then inherited) appears in ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014 A06 (adoption carried forward with NO_ADVANCE) and A10 (mechanism labels mismatched across versions).

findings.title: Cross-agent audit of Claude's V26 run was lost for two rounds; the flawed stream was reused and misattributed
findings.description: Doc: Codex's V26 design (7 Sep) audited Claude's uploaded V26 source and listed defects. 'Its shift schedule includes 406–431 A presentations after B begins → old knowledge is still being trained.' 'Its A probes use new latent identities conditional on labels → old-cohort performance measures rule transfer, not arbitrary old-association recall.' 'A blank input can alter live weights through initial renormalization.' Also: double z-scoring; export columns fixed from a Block-A row, so endpoints were lost; and a 'Pareto improvement' gate that 'allows a retention loss within a margin'. Claude's V27 recommendation then calls that run an 'independent replication' in which 'Two independently designed experiments … agree on both the positive and the negative'. It says 'The Pareto claim was underpowered, not wrong.' Claude's V27 run reused the same V26 shift_stream (V28 provenance). V28 then 'discovers' that 'old-cohort probes are built from … fresh random latent pairs' and retracts the power explanation. Inference: The audit finding existed in the archive one round before. It was not read, or not carried, by the next agent. That caused one wasted round and a misattributed explanation. It is the earliest instance of the retrospective's core failure: a limitation is stated locally and then lost in the next design.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/df55e827c7543e3f_v27_experiment_recommendation.md (orig v27_experiment_recommendation.md) §1.1 'independent replication'; §3 'The Pareto claim was underpowered, not wrong'

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/9a09a44b5e7f7c29_v28_experiment_recommendation.md (orig v28_experiment_recommendation.md) §2.2–2.3; provenance 'reusing the V25 bank substrate and V26 shift stream'
findings.how_detected: Codex source audit (v26 design §3). Claude later rediscovered the defect independently (v28 §2.3) without citing the audit.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every new design must start with an inherited-findings ledger. It quotes every audit finding and limitation recorded against the code, stream or run it reuses, and marks each as resolved, open or accepted. Tooling should refuse to reuse a generator or stream that has open audit findings unless the design explicitly acknowledges them. Calling a run 'independent' requires a different implementation with no shared open defects.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014 core finding: limitations stated in local reports were not carried into the next design.

findings.title: A composite retention/transfer endpoint with no new-acquisition gate rewards stopping learning (HYBRID-FROZEN = 1.000)
findings.description: Doc: V40 defines 'wall = min(retention, delayed held-out transfer, E1 one-shot transfer), all on the untouched wave-A cohort'. Its G0 checks only wave-A acquisition. The nondeployable HYBRID-FROZEN arm (superposed layer frozen after wave A) scores wall 1.000 at loads 64, 128 and 256. HYBRID (0.906/0.596/0.443) is nonetheless reported as 'qualified'. Claude's V39 likewise gated only 'A initial'. The V35–V38 protocols had required D-current ≥90%. V43 (Codex) later found that the slot memory 'can retain old answers while failing to consolidate enough new knowledge … Successful old-memory probes alone therefore do not establish continued learning.' CORE_RECOVERY (17 Sep) separately found the V79E–V85E evolution 'contaminated' by blanket old-memory objectives: 'It must not reward blanket retention merely because a memory is old.' Inference: The V40 report does not mention that its stop-learning control beats the candidate on the primary endpoint. That is direct evidence that the endpoint can be gamed by refusing new learning.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/f3c8dc8952b58bf8_REPORT.md (orig v40_results/REPORT.md): wall table HYBRID-FROZEN 1.000/1.000/1.000; G0 checks A initial only; verdict qualified

PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/d7d7cdefe31c1cc3_v43_analysis_report.md (orig preserved_preV50_designs_from_archives/v43_complete_handoff/v43_analysis_report.md): Q0 failure at loads 128–512 while old recall was about 99%
findings.how_detected: Not detected in V40. Inference from the V40 table. The general class was detected later by V43 Q0 (Codex) and the CORE_RECOVERY reanalysis.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every retention endpoint must be paired with a gate on new or current acquisition and revision. Before running, score a fixed panel of degenerate learners against the endpoint: stop learning after A, frozen layer, exact lookup table, hash table, always the same answer. If any degenerate learner passes or beats the candidate, the endpoint is invalid. Any nondeployable control that beats the candidate must be flagged in the headline.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. CORE_RECOVERY (blanket retention in evolution), FB1/V9.5–V9.7 (taught-cue retention as primary), and ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A01 (learning objective shrunk to taught-association retention, 21–26 Sep, recurring after the contract).

findings.title: Inert interventions and controls reported as results without a no-op check
findings.description: Doc: In V23, retrieve_hard8 and retrieve_soft8 show endpoints identical to ordinary (53.94/99.77/59.26/100.00/36.66). In V20, all five fly arms (exact, compressed, shuffled, outcome-only, feedback-disabled) are identical in every seed. Only the separate review noticed and checked that 'The controller is running'. In the three-mechanism round, withheld-relation contrasts for Z1 and T2 were '+0.0 [+0.0, +0.0]'. The R2/Z1 correction then states the run 'was found to have a nonfunctional N_old_rel control'. In A10, the EA and J contrasts have 'zero empirical variance'. My CSV check of V23: retrieve_hard8 and retrieve_soft8 equal ordinary on every accuracy column in all 6 seeds. Only peak_mutable_numeric_bytes differs (3072 vs 9344). Hard equals soft at 32 slots as well. Inference: The V23 report and later recommendations never flag the retrieval mechanism as non-engaging. Its extra memory cost is charged against an arm that did nothing.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/6507a43c7c900d33_REPORT.md (orig elm_fly_v23_20260906_173231_28825/REPORT.md): identical rows for ordinary, retrieve_hard8 and retrieve_soft8
PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/1bca2a1bde276923_SUMMARY.csv (orig elm_fly_v23_.../SUMMARY.csv): per-seed equality except mutable bytes
findings.how_detected: V20: independent results review. Three-mechanism: a later corrective design. V23: not detected in the archive; my per-seed CSV comparison.
findings.generic_safeguard: Run an automatic inert-arm detector before reporting. Flag any arm whose endpoint vector equals its parent's within 1e-12 across all seeds, and any contrast with a zero-width interval. An arm reported as a mechanism must show a positive engagement diagnostic (nonzero counterfactual effect on the same prestate). A control must show it actually blocks the claimed writes (a literal write ledger). Zero variance means NOT_EVALUABLE unless a structural proof exists before science.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. Package A/B no-write branch defects (ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE 'Package A/B 的禁写分支缺陷'); CLAUDE_A_V3 'Package B V2 E3 stays invalid'.

findings.title: Causality leak (historical lookahead) in Claude's V39 phase code went unflagged in V39 and V40
findings.description: Doc: Codex's V41 design: 'Recover the original Claude V39 PhaseFront … Correct historical lookahead by discovering period only from 146 already observed disjoint warmup records.' The V39 and V40 reports describe the runs as 'Label-free: the only teaching signal is the next-byte residual'. The phase-code arms S3, S4 and S5 drove V40's conclusion that 'stationarity dominates' separation. V52 caught a sibling leak before running: a 2000-byte calibration prefix with '2000 mod 14 = 12 … Resetting it to zero would silently reveal alignment'. Inference: 'Label-free' was checked, but causal-in-time information was not. Using future stream structure for representation calibration is a separate leak class.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/bf66d97e7165c883_v40_experiment_recommendation.md §1.3 stationarity conclusion built on phase arms
findings.how_detected: The other agent's source recovery while implementing the next round (V41). V52: refinement audit before running.
findings.generic_safeguard: Run a mandatory future-mutation test. Change bytes after time t and assert that every representation, calibration statistic and prediction at time ≤t is bit-identical. Also assert that calibration and warmup lengths are whole cycles, or that phase origin is carried causally. 'Label-free' and 'causal' are separate checks.
findings.recurs_later: Within this era: V52 (caught before the run); BYTE_LEARNER v8 R1/R2 (read not read-only; the sequential readout mixed in just-arrived feedback).

findings.title: Evaluator cohort mislabel: 'A_untouched' probes covered the revised and noisy identities (V51); other mis-attributed diagnostics
findings.description: Doc: V52 §2.1: 'revised A identities = first quarter; one-off-noise = second quarter; truly untouched = second half. However, several V51 probes later labelled A_untouched… use the first half, which is exactly revised + noisy.' Corrected 'in measurement only'. Related cases: (a) V39 rec: 'I initially reported to Mr. Zhou that max_members was 1… That is the EXACT-V trajectory'. (b) V9.8: the 12/72 address statistic used only prefix 0, while teaching used four prefixes; the post-run replay gives 42/72. Inference: The primary retention endpoint was computed on the wrong population, and the label hid it. Cohort membership was hand-coded in the evaluator rather than derived from the generator.
findings.how_detected: Refinement of the next design (V52) and self-correction in later recommendations.
findings.generic_safeguard: Evaluator populations must be derived programmatically from generator definitions, e.g. untouched = A \ (revised ∪ noisy). Each probe set needs a unit test asserting disjointness and nonzero size. Any number reported to the user must name the arm and trajectory it comes from.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown from this archive. The V52 fix applied to measurement only, so V51 conclusions stand uncorrected unless re-derived.

findings.title: Synthetic test fixtures are cataloged as result reports, with real-result titles and opposite-sign numbers
findings.description: Doc: The FB1-followup technical fixture (qualification/pipeline/REPORT.md) has the same catalog title, '固定容量路由对照与单次写入诊断', as the real result report. It reports 'GEOMETRY_ADVANTAGE' (+8.5 pp and +9.25 pp), while the real result is 'HASH_ADVANTAGE' (geometry8 − hash8 = −6.02 pp). The FB1 v3.2 fixture FINAL_DECISION.md carries the same candidate table and labels as the real FINAL_DECISION.md. The fixture DECISION.json is an aggregate_result_candidate (with technical_fixture_only true inside the file). INDEX.md lists both FB1-followup reports on adjacent lines with identical titles. Inference: An agent summarizing by title or kind, or by grepping FINAL_DECISION, can cite fabricated fixture numbers as science, including the wrong sign.
findings.how_detected: My catalog and index cross-check. The fixtures do carry in-body banners, but catalog metadata does not separate them.
findings.generic_safeguard: Fixtures must go to a separate path namespace (fixtures/), have a distinct kind (technical_fixture) and a title prefix, and be excluded from results indexes. Fixture numbers should be obviously synthetic, for example far outside any plausible range. Summarizers must refuse documents whose body says 'not scientific results'.
findings.recurs_later: Publication-time issue in this 2026-10-23 archive. It affects every future consumer of the catalog.

findings.title: Failed preregistered gates are narrated as 'power' or 'strictness' failures, with proposals to extend seeds and rewrite the gate
findings.description: Doc: V38 fixed Q10 (beat SHUFFLED-PBF, interval excluding zero) and states 'If SHUFFLED-PBF matches PBF, PBF is rejected'. PBF failed Q10. The V39 rec answers: 'V38's Q10 failure is a power failure, not a mechanism failure. PBF is the best point on the frontier.' It proposes rerunning at 16 seeds where 'the existing 8 trajectories are reused by the resume logic, so only 8 are new', and replacing Q10's OR with a single primary. Yet the same document's §8 says 'PBF adds exactly +0.0000 [0, 0] over CORR2 on every behavioural endpoint'. The V40 rec, on ChatGPT's V39 (Q12 and Q13 failed): 'Q12 and Q13 failed on threshold strictness, not mechanism… The headline NOT ESTABLISHED understates its own result.' Q12 was the one-shot sample-efficiency gate ('no more than one external target presentation'), and 2 of 8 seeds failed it. Counter-examples from the same period: V41 says 'The present gates should remain visible as failed outcomes, rather than being weakened after inspection'. V43 says 'Fitting a selected survivor subset or relaxing Q0 after seeing the data would answer a different question.' Inference: Extending a failed run with additional seeds is optional stopping.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/3b5207ea693bf546_v41_analysis_report.md (orig preserved_preV50_designs_from_archives/v41_complete_handoff/analysis/v41_analysis_report.md) 'gates should remain visible as failed outcomes'
findings.how_detected: Visible only by comparing the protocol, the summary and the next recommendation. No reviewer flagged it at the time.
findings.generic_safeguard: A failed gate is final for that experiment. Narratives may add 'possible reasons', but the verdict, its label and the downstream decision cannot change. A follow-up must use fresh seeds only, never extend an existing run. It needs a new preregistration that names the earlier failure, and the result is reported as a separate experiment. Gate redesigns take effect only for future experiments.
findings.recurs_later: Same pattern of reinterpreting failed or inconclusive gates: ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A06 (adopted core with NO_ADVANCE and zero confirmation worlds).

findings.title: Closure claims ('storage solved', 'class closed') overrode the source reports' own caveats
findings.description: Doc: V23: 'A best-of-many result needs subsequent confirmation; the tested variants do not eliminate entire mechanism families.' V24: 'A failed representative does not eliminate its mechanism family.' Claude's V26 rec: 'The storage problem is solved well enough to stop working on it… What is closed — do not revisit… The mechanism space for storage is exhausted', based on unadjusted six-seed screens. Codex's V26 design replied: 'They do not establish that storage is solved.' The V28 rec: 'That class of mechanism is closed. Do not test another selection heuristic.' The V39 rec: 'selection heuristics … failed matched controls six times'. Inference: Closure language travelled into the next designs as hard exclusions ('Not in scope'). The source reports' limitation statements did not travel with it.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/MECHANISM_SCREEN_20261007/VERSION_REGISTER_20261011/sources/02_REPORT.md (orig elm_fly_v24_20260906_191734_29987/REPORT.md) 'A failed representative does not eliminate its mechanism family'
PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/16589886a21035e0_v26_representation_memory_design.md §2 'do not establish that storage is solved'
findings.how_detected: Partly countered by the other agent (Codex V26 design). Otherwise found by comparing documents.
findings.generic_safeguard: A closure or exclusion statement must cite the scope the source report allows: tested representative, workload, n, adjusted or not. Phrases such as 'closed', 'solved' or 'exhausted' are invalid unless the source report uses them. Exclusion lists must carry each entry's evidence level and an expiry or reopen condition.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A10: '停止具体配方不等于排除整个机制家族' (stopping one recipe does not exclude the whole mechanism family); mechanism ledgers had mismatched closure entries.

findings.title: A protection guard too wide ever to show harm let candidates ADVANCE
findings.description: Doc: FB1 v3.2 used a Hoeffding retention-risk interval with half-widths of 38.43 pp (canonical) and 33.28 pp (high load). All of FB2, FB4 and FB8 got 'STABLE_RISK_UNRESOLVED … ADVANCE_AS_RESOURCE_CANDIDATE'. The v3.1 hostile audit had computed that ±5 pp would need about 5,696 worlds per panel. It also warned that the original rule let even confirmed harm advance. The minimal-core v2 audit: 'no confirmed harm' is not the same as harm small enough to accept; an interval from −6 to +4 can pass. In POST_V5_FULL_V3, 139 of 152 K8 worlds had items B got right and S_LOCAL got wrong, yet the label was 'NO_CONFIRMED_GUARD_HARM … 进入后续研究 (advance to follow-up): True'. Inference: The veto was unreachable by design. The ADVANCE label therefore rested on the primary endpoint alone, while the reports correctly said 'unresolved is not safe'.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/88f0636e55be8429_REPORT.md (orig reviews/fixed_bank_v3_1_hostile_audit_20260921/REPORT.md) '约需 5,696个世界/面板' (about 5,696 worlds per panel); §1 confirmed harm could still advance
findings.how_detected: Hostile pre-run audits (21 Sep) flagged it. The design kept the guard and reported risk as unresolved.
findings.generic_safeguard: Before the run, compute each guard's interval width at the planned n. If the guard cannot detect harm of practically relevant size, its status is UNASSESSED, not 'no confirmed harm'. A primary-only ADVANCE then needs an explicit owner override. Report guard power next to every promotion label.
findings.recurs_later: Same class: promotion and adoption labels granted without independent confirmation (ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A06 COV-SUPPORT, confirmation worlds 0).

findings.title: Unit fact 'exact or hash addressing retains but destroys transfer' (V32–V40) was re-derived in the native line (V9.7–V9.8)
findings.description: Doc: V32–V34: the exact-context dictionary keeps 100% retention and 0% revision. V39: 'HASH-O destroys input similarity (ratio ~1) and is the retention corner', with retention 1.000 and held-out 0.000. V40 rec: 'Retention tracks different-key overlap; transfer tracks same-key overlap.' Three weeks later, V9.7 kept HASH8 as 'an absolute-performance component worth further diagnosis' because of higher taught-pair accuracy. V9.8 then found HASH8 E3 at −8.3 and −19.4 pp and concluded: 'HASH8's strong exact-pair scores alongside weak held-out scores show why V9.7's higher taught-pair accuracy cannot serve as the project's core criterion.' FB1-followup found hash beating geometric routing at 8 banks (−6.02 pp), noting that the result applies only to exact-repeat encoding tasks. Inference: The ELM-era result was never carried into the native program's design rationale. It was learned again at the cost of a 256-world V9.7 run and the V9.8 trial.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/designs/2fdf5316b293447c_SOURCE_PROTOCOL.md (orig WorkstreamFB1_Followup_v1/SOURCE_PROTOCOL.md) §3.1 '仅适用于精确重复编码任务' (applies only to exact-repeat encoding tasks)
findings.how_detected: Re-derived empirically in V9.8. The connection to V39 is my inference; no native-line document cites V39.
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a cross-lineage unit-fact registry: claim, evidence path, scope and a failure signature. Before adopting a component, a design must query the registry for conflicts (for example 'hash route → zero held-out transfer') and state why it expects otherwise.
findings.recurs_later: Generic IO later used 'exact context hash' banks (ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A07). Whether the transfer limit was re-learned there is unknown from this archive.

findings.title: Taught-cue first return and retention (E1) became the primary and ADVANCE basis before any held-out gate (native line, 17–26 Sep)
findings.description: Doc: The primary endpoints of CORE_RECOVERY, FB1 and POST_V5_FULL_V3 were 'high-load first-return' or retention of explicitly taught cues. V9.5–V9.7 measured old-pair choice on previously rewarded pairs. The 26 Sep objective contract states: 'The V9.4–V9.7 old-memory loss endpoint is loss of choice or margin on previously rewarded ordered-byte pairs … Neither establishes E3 transfer.' It cites a 'V88_TO_V9_7_OBJECTIVE_DRIFT_AUDIT_20260926.md' that is absent from the repository. Inference: The objective shrank from 'useful later reuse' to 'retain taught cues'. Each local report was honest, but the program was steering toward E1.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/8ad93977a33314a9_REPORT.md 'cannot serve as the project's core criterion'
minifly_b/package/DOCS/MINIFLY_OBJECTIVE_CONTRACT.md 'Current interpretation and next decision'; link to the missing drift audit
findings.how_detected: The 26 Sep objective audit and contract, after V9.7.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every design must declare its evidence level E0–E4 and include a recitation-countermodel table. An E1 endpoint cannot carry a promotion or ADVANCE label toward the core objective. A run-time check should compare the primary endpoint's evidence level with the stated program objective.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A01: '后续仍复发，说明纠偏文件没有持续约束研究决策' (it recurred afterwards, so the correction document did not keep constraining research decisions).

findings.title: 'Generalization' claims in V36–V40 were E2-level surface re-rendering, presented as one-shot generalization
findings.description: Doc: V36 protocol: 'Two renderings of the same key differ only in header and separator and share 10 of 12 raw causal bytes'. V40 rec presents superposed 'E1 one-shot transfer 0.998' as 'immediate generalization' and 'complementary-learning-systems structure arrived at empirically'. The 26 Sep contract: 'Re-rendering the same semantic cue/pair under a new wrapper remains E2… not general rule or new-task transfer.' Inference: The held-out alias in these rounds is a near-duplicate context. Transfer through code overlap is surface similarity, not relational generalization from learned units. The architecture narrative (CLS, fast/slow) was built on E2 evidence.
findings.how_detected: Inference, by applying the later contract retroactively.
findings.generic_safeguard: For every 'held-out' probe, report the raw-byte and code overlap with the nearest trained context. Any probe whose only novelty is a re-rendering of a taught item is labelled E2. 'Generalization' wording requires E3: unseen combinations or relations with a prior-teaching causal control.
findings.recurs_later: The contract formalized this distinction later. Whether E2 continued to be labelled 'generalization' afterwards is outside this era.

findings.title: Version-namespace collisions: different agents ran different experiments under one version label
findings.description: Doc: V26: 'The independent runner has a different filename and source identity; the two experiments' trajectories and gates must not be merged under one version label.' V37: 'Two different experiments were called V36 and must not be conflated.' V27 and V39 each had a ChatGPT run and a Claude run with different designs, and recommendations pooled them as 'confirmed twice' or 'three separate runs now agree'. V31 is a Claude MESU run (in the archive), while the V35 refined design describes a V31 that 'transferred the full-covariance mechanism'. Inference: Shared labels encouraged cross-run pooling and 'independent replication' claims across implementations with different stream defects (see E02).
findings.how_detected: Noticed by the agents themselves (V26 design, V37 protocol), but never fixed structurally.
findings.generic_safeguard: An experiment ID must embed agent, source hash and design hash (for example V36-codex-38de31). Pooling across IDs is allowed only through a declared meta-analysis. 'Replication' requires the same locked protocol and an independent implementation without shared open defects.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A10 (mechanism IDs mismatched across 108/136/254/71 views) and A08 ('old core' meaning changed twice).

findings.title: Adoption without confirmation, followed by decline: the contrast-encoder default and the 'validated' covariance primitive
findings.description: Doc: V27 rec: 'Adopt contrast/residual-contrast as the encoder default' from unadjusted screens. V28: 'Contrast geometry is confirmed a third time… Contrast is the encoder default.' On the byte stream, V31 P0 found the 'contrast' code has bits/symbol worse than uniform: 'Code carries no task information. All mechanism verdicts VOID.' Covariance: V33 found +16.4 pp 'on known V32 seeds, not independent confirmation'. V34 fresh seeds gave H-P 15.62% vs H-O 7.03% (+8.6). The V35 refined design calls it 'a validated interference-reduction primitive', yet V35 C0 gives +3.12 [−0.82, 7.07], 'favorable_unresolved_precision'. Inference: Each adoption ran ahead of confirmation. The V31 'contrast' arm is probably the V27/V28 contrast family; this is not proven in the archive.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/e1eab09edf596959_SUMMARY.md (orig v33_x/SUMMARY.md) 'reused V32 seeds … not fresh confirmation'
findings.how_detected: V31's P0 adequacy gate, and the V35 preregistered C0 replication.
findings.generic_safeguard: Status vocabulary should be SCREENED, then CONFIRMED (fresh seeds, locked), then TRANSFERRED (new workload P0 passed). A default or 'validated' label requires CONFIRMED. A component carried into a new workload requires a fresh adequacy (P0) check before mechanisms are tested on it.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A06 (COV-SUPPORT adopted with zero confirmation worlds; adoption then not carried to the next substrate).

findings.title: An absolute gate taken from biology was unreachable on the workload, and the later rationale for dropping it was false
findings.description: Doc: The V36 fly preflight required J_same ≥0.30, J_diff ≤0.04 and R_J ≥10. It failed ('fly_separation_gate_failed') and a fully implemented arm never ran. The V39 rec called it 'unreachable on this workload regardless of code quality… The preflight therefore measured the workload, not the hypothesis'. The V40 rec: S5 reached ratio 11.01, J_diff 0.032, J_same 0.350, 'clearing all three… on the workload where that gate was declared unreachable. Clearing it bought nothing… it was reachable.' V52 later: 'The earlier draft allowed a cross-talk/Jaccard threshold to decide… That is too strong. Every stationary deployable arm receives Block B.' Inference: The gate was not checked for feasibility on the actual inputs, and the post-hoc 'mis-specified' story was wrong. Both failure modes recurred around one gate.
findings.how_detected: Self-correction across V39 → V40 → V52.
findings.generic_safeguard: Absolute thresholds imported from another system need a feasibility witness on the actual workload: a constructed code that passes, or a computed ceiling. Representation-geometry gates should be diagnostics, not vetoes on behavioral tests. A claim that a gate was 'unreachable' needs a proof, not an argument.
findings.recurs_later: Within this era it was fixed in V52 §13. Later recurrence is unknown.

findings.title: A gate built to protect the author's own prediction hid the strongest contrary result
findings.description: Doc: Claude's V26 rec predeclared that afferent selection and sparsification (A, B) would 'dominate' temporal order (C). Codex on Claude's run: the residual temporal filter improved structured accuracy by 10.84 pp [6.49, 15.19], winning all six seeds, but 'Its report's gate excludes the temporal arm by name and therefore fails to surface this important comparison.' The Claude V26 Block-A gate table lists only A×B cells. Its Block-B 'pareto_improvement' label was given while one-shot accuracy fell significantly (−1.41 [−1.84, −0.97]). Inference: The gate design itself encoded the hypothesis being tested (confirmation bias). This is distinct from changing gates after outcomes.
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent source and results audit (Codex).
findings.generic_safeguard: The gate set must include the primary contrast for every predeclared competing hypothesis, not only the favored one. A 'Pareto' or 'compatibility' label requires every component's lower bound to be at or above its margin. A significant loss on any declared endpoint cannot coexist with a Pareto label.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown beyond this era.

findings.title: Invalid or no-op controls caught before the run by hostile audits
findings.description: Doc: post_v5_full_low audit: (a) a fixed bank-label permutation applied consistently to reads and writes is '换编号，不是改变哪些输入共享存储' (relabeling, not a change in which inputs share storage), so original and control are behaviorally equivalent. (b) C1's 'historical formula' did not match elm_omnibus10.py lines 565–595. (c) Dose conservation before B does not imply actual slow-dose conservation after B (shown with an algebraic counterexample). (d) Revision was missing from the protection vector, 'can protect old answers by writing less'. (e) A tail metric minus a self-baseline that is always zero became an implicit zero-loss gate. fixed_bank_v2 audit: configure(banks=K) changes the centres too, which would break the fixed-address constraint. The historical exclusion scanner missed the other root directory. Replay budget arithmetic was wrong (8×2=16, not 8). CLAUDE_A_V3: Z2_rand was not truly yoked (+5.07% dose) until re-implemented.
findings.how_detected: Hostile audits that read actual source lines and recomputed arithmetic (a practice that worked).
findings.generic_safeguard: For every control, provide a written proof or test that it changes the claimed variable and nothing else: a non-identity test, a yoked-dose equality test, and a source-equation match with file:line. Run these as fixtures before any science world is generated.
findings.recurs_later: Yes, in that control and branch defects continued (Package A/B no-write branch defects in the retrospective).

findings.title: Fail-open validators and gate code: missing or NaN inputs passed
findings.description: Doc: V43 reporting review: 'missing comparisons [turn] into Q7 pass. This is an actual fail-open gate'. 'A positive firewall-check count establishes that at least one check ran, not that every byte was checked.' The omnibus F silently reduced the hypothesis under rank deficiency. V9.5 receipt re-audit: 'the frozen validator… accepts a choice of 2.0, a NaN scalar margin, and an impossible [99,99,99] overlap label.' FULL v3 readiness: a missing or NaN guard cannot show harm, so it would auto-advance. CLAUDE_A_V3: 'a self-consistent joint change … is accepted by the log audit and rejected by the replay.'
findings.how_detected: Independent pre-freeze code review (V43); a post-run receipt re-audit with synthetic corruptions (V9.5); a replay-based tamper test (A_V3).
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate code must be fail-closed: missing, NaN or out-of-range inputs give NOT_EVALUABLE and never PASS. Mutation-test every gate with synthetic missing, NaN, out-of-range and self-consistent tampered inputs. Coverage checks must count equal to the denominator. Audits must replay the equations independently, not only check log consistency.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown beyond this era.

findings.title: Absolute gains misread as protection; relative contrasts misread as recovery
findings.description: Doc: V9.6: the generic results REPORT shows FB4 +7.92 pp [+1.11, +14.72] vs REF. The decision REPORT for the same run shows the difference-in-differences '+0.42 pp [−6.10, +6.93]' and 'almost all of its old-choice advantage is already present before the four new cohorts'. V9.7: HASH8 is +10.42 pp absolute, but its DID is −11.20 pp (greater write harm) because it 'start[s] from a much stronger old-memory state'. V9.5: the original report says a 24 h rest 'undoes only part of' the cost. The receipt re-audit: 'The WWWW old-choice mean does not improve… narrows mostly because the no-new-write arm loses its temporary advantage.' Inference: FB1's +25.9 pp FB8 first-return gain (ADVANCE) was not decomposed into birth advantage versus write-harm reduction.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/results/802e79d1c8cfe876_REPORT.md (orig BYTE_CORE_V9_5/run/REPORT.md; FULL151 era) 'a 24 h rest undoes only part of it'
findings.how_detected: Design-level DID planning (V9.7 design); receipt re-audit (V9.5).
findings.generic_safeguard: Every protection claim must report the absolute level, the own-state DID, the prechallenge level, and a matched-precorrect-item analysis. A relative contrast that changes must be decomposed into its two arms before it is interpreted.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown beyond this era.

findings.title: Unrecorded pivot: V47's preregistered next branch was ignored and the objective statement changed
findings.description: Doc: V47 §20, if G4 fails: 'Close this representation branch… The next mainline branch becomes… short-context-surprise-gated distributed slow plasticity.' V47 G4 failed. V48 and V49 instead test raw-BANC motifs. They restate the objective as 'a minimal, bounded-state, non-Transformer, online persistent-learning core whose architecture is materially constrained by the raw fly connectome'. V45's objective had included 'generalizes beyond exact presentations', which is absent from the V48/V49 statement. Neither V48 nor V49 mentions V47 or any authorization. Separately, boundedness was deferred four rounds while verdicts read 'qualified': V35 'Stage II is unbounded exact-context storage'; V36 'Bounded capacity is deferred'; V37/V38 'Storage remains unbounded'. V39 rec: '64 facts cost 9.5 MB and 3.5 G multiply-adds'. Inference: The change may reflect a user instruction that was not recorded. The archive does not show it.
findings.how_detected: My cross-document comparison. Grep finds no V47 reference in V48/V49.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every design must diff its objective text against the canonical contract. Any change must cite the user's instruction (date and quote). Any departure from a previous design's preregistered next-branch rule must be recorded with its rationale. Core constraints such as boundedness cannot be deferred for more than one round without moving into the primary gate.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE A05 (priority drift toward noise handling) and A03/A07 (substrate changed without inheritance contracts).

findings.title: Unit fact about the 104-port code scale was found in V20 and rediscovered in V49
findings.description: Doc: The V20 review showed that random orthogonal 104-port codes give C Cᵀ = 104 I and dilute output-gain effects to a 0.8–2.0% operator deviation. V22 then factored W = VC to avoid 'task-invisible output directions'. V49 reused rate 0.6 with a normalized 104-dimensional MBON code: 'directly reusing the old one-hot rate 0.6 with a normalized 104-dimensional code produced an artificially small teaching coordinate', fixed by an engineering sqrt(104) standardization and eta = 4.0. Inference: The scaling fact was re-derived, not looked up. It was caught by engineering seeds this time.
findings.how_detected: Engineering-seed calibration in V49.
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a numerical-scale registry (codebook dimension versus update scale) in the unit-fact registry. Interfaces that change output coding must state the residual scale and include a 'teaching coordinate magnitude' check before science.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown.

findings.title: Source-hash provenance gap for the official V26 run
findings.description: Doc: The V26 design §16: 'The source's SHA256 is 1263a33ea101036ce267b0226269bef4b251f5d575745c8f7486b5e71792a22b… The full 1,350-trajectory primary-plus-confirmation experiment remains for the user's run.' The completed 1,350/1,350 report and the V27 rec cite source SHA256 45fcf4f7…82068b. Neither document explains the difference. Inference: The executed source is not the verified, shipped one, or the design hash is stale. In either case, whether the run used the verified code cannot be established from the archive.
findings.how_detected: My hash cross-check.
findings.generic_safeguard: Before analysis, the runner must assert that the executing source hash equals the design-locked hash, or record a signed amendment that explains the diff. Reports must print both the locked and the executed hashes.
findings.recurs_later: Later runs added strict source locks (V9.x, A_V3). The gap seems specific to this early ELM period.

findings.title: Upstream recommendations and inputs were lost; implementations proceeded from 'recovered' intent
findings.description: Doc: V41: 'The recovered latest chat recommendation proposed… Its full wording and numerical settings were unavailable.' V42: 'The complete latest brainstorming text and numerical protocol could not be recovered.' CLAUDE_A_V3: 'Muse's source, locks, receipts, stop record, P3 failure receipt and roster amendment were not available'. The objective contract links to V88_TO_V9_7_OBJECTIVE_DRIFT_AUDIT_20260926.md, which is not in the repository. Archive README: 'Trash recovery could not be completed'. Earlier cleanup 'permanently unlinked some generated historical artifacts'. Inference: The agents handled this honestly by labelling 'refinements, not reproduction'. But the design chain had gaps where limitations could be lost without anyone noticing.
findings.how_detected: Stated by the implementing agents themselves.
findings.generic_safeguard: A recommendation is not executable until it is committed to the repository with a hash. Designs must cite the committed recommendation hash. Every link a contract or design references is checked for existence in CI.
findings.recurs_later: Yes. ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE references the same missing drift audit. Source paths in many reports point to non-repository local folders.

findings.title: Catalog era labels come from filename version strings and split design/report pairs
findings.description: Doc: The README keeps chronology 'conservative'. Yet 'EARLY_VERSION_V1_V49' contains Sep 21–30 native Full151-line work: BYTE_CORE_V9_x, FB1, A10/A11, CORE_RECOVERY, MINIFLY_*, CLAUDE_A_V3. It also contains V52 (12 Sep, beyond V49). Pairs are split. BYTE_CORE_V9_10E DESIGN is EARLY but its REPORT is TRANSITION. BYTE_CORE_V9_6 DESIGN is TRANSITION but its REPORT is EARLY. FE1_CASE_V3 DESIGN is TRANSITION, REPORT EARLY. A11 v2 designs are EARLY, their AUDIT TRANSITION. The V9.5 run report (TRANSITION) says 'Under the current FULL_151 value pathway', while its refinement audit and receipt audit are EARLY. Inference: Era-partitioned analyses, like this one and the post-Full151 one, will each see half of a design→result→audit chain. That reproduces the limitation-loss problem at the meta level.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/CATALOG.json items for BYTE_CORE_V9_10E_REPLAY_GEOMETRY, BYTE_CORE_V9_6, MINIFLY_FE1_CASE_V3_20260928, A11_MODULAR_A_REDESIGN_V2*, V52_Mac_M3
findings.how_detected: My catalog grouping by original folder.
findings.generic_safeguard: Group catalog entries by lineage (design → run → report → audit → erratum) and give the whole chain one era label. Infer dates from document headers, not version strings. Era-partitioned reviews must pull every member of a chain that touches their era.
findings.recurs_later: An artifact of this 2026-10-23 publication. It affects the current analysis split.

findings.title: Zero-variance and structural-identity rules did not stick from Sep 21 to Sep 28
findings.description: Doc: A10 (21 Sep): 'zero empirical variance; unresolved without invariant'. BKR v5 precision: 'Zero variance without a deterministic proof remains inconclusive.' The three-mechanism report (28 Sep) still prints '+0.0 [+0.0, +0.0]' intervals as results. The R2/Z1 correction (29 Sep) restates the rule: 'A zero empirical variance does not justify a zero-width success interval.' A10 also labels contrasts of 2.4e-7 and −4.8e-7 margin units 'positive' and 'negative' with 'No equivalence or materiality threshold … specified'. Good counter-practice: V42 and v3.1 explicitly called equalities and monotone collisions 'structural, not findings'.
findings.how_detected: Document comparison. The rule was restated after the failure.
findings.generic_safeguard: The shared statistics library enforces it: zero variance gives NOT_EVALUABLE unless a structural proof is attached; sign labels require a declared materiality threshold. Reports cannot hand-format intervals outside the library.
findings.recurs_later: Recurred within this era (28 Sep). Later status is unknown.

findings.title: E3 evidence in the native line is narrow: one-bit or scalar ceilings, external decoders above native, and a cyclic-family failure
findings.description: Doc: The V9.8/V9.9A class task 'can be solved by a one-bit class per symbol'. V9.9B passes primary E3 (+9.57 pp) but fails the 'graded-beyond-one-bit' gate (one-bit oracle ceiling 75%). V9.9C: extra writes help taught pairs (+9.69 pp) far more than held-out pairs (+1.76 pp). V9.10A: an external graph potential reaches 76.17% vs 60.74% for the native read. V9.10C: an engineered shared head reaches 77.54%, an interval that includes the 75% one-bit ceiling. V9.10D cyclic family (scalar ceiling 6/9): the head scores 51.04% and native 47.40%, a 'clean negative'. R2/Z1: native Z0 W−N is +38% on a fixture 'a one-bit-per-symbol class rule could solve'. The reports label these limits carefully. Inference: The route retrospective's positive-evidence section cites V9.9A/B as Full151 generalization. That is valid only at the narrow level the reports state. External decoder scores must never be cited as learner ability.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014/REPORT.md '必须保留的正面证据' (positive evidence that must be kept)
findings.how_detected: Analytic countermodel ceilings that the reports themselves computed (a practice that worked).
findings.generic_safeguard: Every E3 fixture must publish its countermodel ceilings (exact table, one-bit class, scalar potential, win count). Promotion requires beating the strongest non-trivial ceiling, plus a relation family that a scalar potential cannot solve. External probes must be tagged EXTERNAL_DECODER and excluded from learner-capability summaries.
findings.recurs_later: The retrospective uses V9.9A/B as positive evidence, correctly scoped there. Downstream summaries risk inflating them.

findings.title: Aggregate metrics that hide the target: whole-stream loss, win frequency, ratio-of-means versus mean-of-ratios
findings.description: Doc: V32 made 'whole-stream AND target-only prequential losses mandatory' because 'the target is only one of 14 bytes'. Its results: the dictionary has the worst whole bpb (2.857) but the best target bpb (0.818) and 100% retention, while 'full' has the best whole bpb. V43: 'Slow predictions won the binary per-event comparison on 55.46% of G events, yet their pooled loss was 5.67510 bits/G versus 3.64936… The frequency of wins therefore hides the size of costly misses.' V43 also found that 'Only 354/85,769 online G events—0.41%—were designated identity targets', so diagnostic training covered a different population. The v3.1 audit: per-query ratio means and pooled-mass ratios differ (50% vs 1% example), so the aggregation must be locked.
findings.how_detected: Design-time foresight (V32) and post-run diagnostics (V43).
findings.generic_safeguard: Every aggregate endpoint must name its population and aggregation (mean of ratios versus ratio of sums). Report target-only and non-target components separately. Any learned arbiter or diagnostic must report its training-population versus test-population mismatch.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown.

findings.title: Audit and review practices: what worked and what failed
findings.description:
Doc, worked:
- Pre-run hostile audits recomputed arithmetic and read source lines (the 21 Sep reviews).
- V43 wrote an erratum before science that corrected a false claim that 'capture can exceed 1'.
- The V43 reporting review found fail-open gates.
- The V9.5 receipt re-audit recomputed 1,167 fields and found validator defects.
- The V42 final_results_audit reconstructed 12,000 probe rows.
- V9.10A–D hashed predictions before scoring.
- V43 failed on its Q0 validity gate with no rescue from surviving subsets.
- The FB1-followup launch gate stopped before launch when the storage estimate was 3.87× over budget instead of deleting evidence.
- V9.9A added a post-run check that the new cohort was actually learned.
- An independent replay rejected tampering that the log audit accepted.

Doc, failed or limited:
- V9.5 A3: 'The implementer (Claude) is the only reviewer available… labelled implementer-audited'.
- The A11 reviewer corrected its own audit: 'The B at 1.7× slower allowance… was in the wrong direction.'
- POST_V5's 'extra audit missed the report plotting dependency'.
- The V39 G2 'bug fix' was made by the author alone (E01).

Inference: Audits were strongest before the run and on arithmetic. They were weakest in carrying their findings into the next round's recommendation (E02, E09).
findings.how_detected: Direct reading of the audit documents.
findings.generic_safeguard: Make the practices that worked mandatory. Before the run: a hostile audit with file:line evidence. Fail-closed gate fixtures. Predictions hashed before scoring. Independent replay. Stop at the launch gate on resource failure. Add a carry-forward step: the next design must import the audit's open items. If no independent reviewer is available, the result is labelled implementer-audited and cannot be promoted.
findings.recurs_later: The positive practices continued in the native line. Carry-forward failures recurred (ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE).

findings.title: Small engineering errors repeatedly broke the post-science pipeline
findings.description:
Doc:
- POST_V5_FULL_V3: the summary step crashed because matplotlib was missing; STATUS elapsed_seconds recorded the recovery-summary time, not the full experiment time.
- R2/Z1 v1: 'failed before committing any science receipt because the nested world directory did not exist'.
- R2/Z1 v1.1: the analysis 'failed while formatting its Markdown report because lock was not in scope in __main__'.
- V9.8: 'An initial launch was blocked by a source-lock JSON tuple/list mismatch'.
- V41: the three-worker run hit the memory limit, and the broken pool needed a manual interrupt.
- V43: the diagnostic reader rejected the −1 sentinel, needing a separate correction.
- BYTE_LEARNER v8: the 'markov2' baseline used one byte of context, which weakened the comparator.

Inference: Each was disclosed, and none changed frozen science. But each forced ad-hoc completion steps, a point where errors and selective handling can enter.
findings.how_detected: Runtime failures and implementation cross-checks.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every test cycle must run the full end-to-end pipeline on a technical world before science: commit paths, report rendering, plotting dependencies, analysis entrypoints, lock parsing. Use frozen environment manifests. Each baseline needs a unit test proving it implements its named definition (for example, the context order).
findings.recurs_later: Unknown beyond this era. The retrospective mentions run interruptions in Package A/B.

unit_facts: Normalized local delta writes on overlapping sparse features learn and revise quickly but overwrite unrelated old associations. Cumulative ridge retains but under-revises because it keeps counting obsolete targets. Neither meets the persistence-plus-revision goal (V20 review, results/67d35b7d1fa5f061_v20_results_review.md).

Gain modulation of output ports through random 104-port codes barely changes the task-space update operator: ||M−I||/||I|| is about 0.8–2.0%. Code dimension sets the update scale (V20 review). V49 rediscovered this and fixed it with sqrt(104) (designs/40c5c8649c56a6fe §10.1).

An exact-context dictionary keeps 100% retention and 0% revision; shared parametric writers keep 2–22% untouched retention after three interfering waves (V32–V34 summaries, results/ee65f7fb24fc5b00, e1eab09edf596959, 9c79f0f7a3880a2a).

A true cumulative ridge/RLS solver rescues shared retention (95%), but at the cost of current-learning, early-learning and revision gates and much worse target bits per byte (V35 Stage I, results/5cddb9746ab60b7d_SUMMARY.md).

An additive residual over a drifting shared base fails even with exact private storage: LOCAL-R 29.7% vs LOCAL-V 99.2%. Freezing the base restores it (FROZEN-R 100%) (V35, V36: results/5cddb9746ab60b7d, b63f0b2e0ea9f59a).

Retention tracks different-key code overlap and one-shot transfer tracks same-key overlap. Hash or exact addressing gives a retention corner with zero transfer (V39 G4; V40 rec §2). Re-derived in the native line: HASH8 has the best taught-pair retention but no E3 (V9.7/V9.8).
Code stationarity dominates the separation ratio. A code whose normalizer keeps drifting (self-overlap 0.62–0.74) underperforms a stationary low-ratio code (V40 rec §1.3; V41 PHASE-FROZEN vs LIVE).

A valid compatibility or retention task needs: recall-dependent old probes (the same latents as training), arbitrary bindings, headroom for the frozen encoder actually used, and no replay (V28 rec §3).
Encoder adequacy (P0) on the actual stream must be shown before any mechanism test. The 'contrast' default chosen on synthetic tasks carried no information on a symbol stream (V31).

Learning positive invariance in one shared matrix raises useful transfer and harmful different-outcome cross-talk together. Learned downstream pathway routing made the harmful interference worse (V45/V46 summaries and V46/V47 designs §1).

Under fixed slot capacity, old recall can stay at about 99% while acquisition of the newest cohort collapses: mature-slot coverage 4.6% at load 256. Mature-slot pressure is the dominant cause (V43 analysis; V44 SLOT_PRESSURE_DOMINANT).

Adaptive routing hurt compared with fixed routing (S_LOCAL − S_FIXED = −19.05 pp). A random hash beat geometric fixed routing at 8 banks for exact-repeat first return (−6.02 pp). More independent stores mainly add capacity (POST_V5_FULL_V3; FB1-followup).

Extra banks raise absolute old and new choice largely through a birth advantage, but do not reduce incremental write harm: V9.6 DID +0.42 [−6.10, +6.93]; V9.7 HASH8 DID −11.20 pp (results/f8a26f815ea83f5a, 008d8788aee0284b).
Native REF: four overlapping new cohorts cost about 11.3 pp on old taught pairs; 123 of 563 known pairs were lost vs 3 without writing (V9.5 audit).

Native REF shows limited, reproducible within-family E3: +17.2 pp on the class task and +9.6 pp on the rank task, at or below one-bit-per-symbol ceilings. Extra writes improve taught pairs much more than held-out pairs (V9.9A–C).

Native outputs contain more relational information than the native readout uses: an external graph potential reaches 76% vs 61% native; a frozen-KC ridge probe 82%. An online shared delta head on frozen KC codes reaches about 77.5% on rank (scalar-potential solvable) but 51% on cyclic relations (V9.9C, V9.10A, V9.10C, V9.10D).

A single native write gives larger absolute but not truth-aligned impulses to pairs sharing a byte. Early aversive teaching moves the taught pair the wrong way in all four worlds (V9.10B), which points to a valence-dependent write/read quirk.

Held-out aliases in the V36–V40 workloads share 10 of 12 context bytes with trained renderings, and different keys share 6 of 12. 'Transfer' there is surface overlap (E2), not relational E3 (V36 protocol §3.2).
process_observations: The loop in this era had two agents. Claude wrote recommendations, often after reading the other agent's results. ChatGPT/Codex locked protocols, implemented, and audited the uploaded Claude code. Corrections were real and frequent, but they appeared as sections of the NEXT design ('Corrections to Claude', 'Corrections to my own earlier claims'). They were not attached as errata to the reports they corrected.

Recommendation documents are where limitations get lost. Reports and locked protocols in this era are mostly careful. Closure claims, reinterpretations of failed gates, and 'independent replication' claims all appear in recommendation documents that set the next agenda.

The strongest artifacts are the 21 Sep Chinese hostile audits. They read source lines, recompute arithmetic, power and storage, find structural identities, and give minimal revision lists. They audited designs; comparable post-run audits arrived only with V9.5 (26 Sep).

Staged gates ordered as validity, then mechanism (P0/G0/Q0, 'a failure voids the levels beneath it') were adopted early (V27 headroom, V31 P0, V39 G0–G2) and work when they are applied to the CURRENT acquisition, not only to initial acquisition.

Resource and qualification gates often blocked or delayed science. A11 v3.8.3 never instantiated its grid. The FB1-followup launch gate stopped on storage. A11 was redesigned to 'one-hour packets' at the user's request. This protected evidence integrity but produced long chains of non-science iterations.

The user's stated preferences shaped scope: larger samples (FULL over LOW), small bundles under 10 MB, 'one-hour questions'. The archive does not record the user decisions behind some pivots (V47 → V48 raw-BANC; the ELM → native transition), which makes objective drift hard to separate from authorized redirection.
Workloads were synthetic throughout: 14-byte records, A→B→C→D waves, 264 identities from V20 to V27, loads of at most 512. Scaling was repeatedly deferred ('Scaling untested since V20').
The catalog's era split mixes chronologies. The early-era label contains both ELM work (6–12 Sep) and native Full151-line work (17–30 Sep). Analysts should read whole lineage chains, not single eras.

skill_recommendations.name: inherited-findings-ledger
skill_recommendations.rule: Before writing any design or recommendation, list every audit finding, limitation and erratum recorded against each artifact the design reuses (code, stream, run, verdict). Quote each with its path, and mark it RESOLVED (with evidence), OPEN, or ACCEPTED (with rationale). Refuse to reuse a generator, stream or result that has OPEN items unless the design names them in its threats section.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E02 (Codex's V26 audit was lost for two rounds), E09 (caveats dropped in favour of closure claims), and the route retrospective's core finding that limitations are not carried forward.

skill_recommendations.name: verdict-change-erratum-protocol
skill_recommendations.rule: Any change to a reported verdict after outcomes requires: (1) an erratum file next to the original, showing the old and new verdict and the code diff; (2) a classification of BUG_FIX if the arm, endpoint and loads are unchanged and only computation errors were fixed, or POST_HOC otherwise; (3) for POST_HOC, no upgrade of the verdict; (4) sign-off by a different agent; (5) distinct titles in all indexes. Downstream documents must cite the erratum ID.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E01: the V39 corrected report flipped the verdict by re-selecting arm, endpoint and loads, with no erratum, an identical title, and immediate downstream reliance.

skill_recommendations.name: failed-gate-finality
skill_recommendations.rule: A failed preregistered gate is final for that experiment. Narratives may list hypotheses for why it failed but cannot relabel the result 'power failure' or 'strictness' in any decision field. Follow-ups use fresh seeds only, never extend an existing run, and carry a new preregistration that cites the failure. Gate rewrites take effect only for future experiments.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E08: V38 Q10 and ELM V39 Q12/Q13 were reinterpreted, with proposals to reuse existing trajectories plus new seeds and to change the gate's OR structure.

skill_recommendations.name: degenerate-learner-endpoint-audit
skill_recommendations.rule: For every primary endpoint, compute before the run the score of a fixed panel of degenerate or shortcut learners: stop learning after phase A, frozen layer, exact-key table, canonicalized-key table, hash table, one-bit class rule, scalar potential, constant answer. If any of them passes the gate or beats the candidate, the endpoint is invalid or limited to the corresponding evidence level. Nondeployable controls that beat the candidate must appear in the headline.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E03 (HYBRID-FROZEN wall = 1.000), E12/E13 (E1 and E2 endpoints driving promotion), E27 (one-bit and scalar ceilings).

skill_recommendations.name: inert-arm-and-control-detector
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any report is written, flag automatically: (a) arms whose endpoint vectors equal the parent's within 1e-12 across all seeds; (b) zero-width intervals; (c) controls whose literal write ledger does not differ from the treatment in the claimed domain; (d) counterfactual same-prestate effects of exactly zero for a supposed mechanism. A flagged arm cannot be reported as a mechanism result until a positive engagement check passes.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E04: V23 retrieval arms are bit-identical to ordinary; V20 fly arms identical; the three-mechanism [+0.0,+0.0] with a nonfunctional N_old_rel; A10 zero variance.

skill_recommendations.name: causal-time-firewall-test
skill_recommendations.rule: For every learner and every calibration or normalization step, run a future-mutation test: change all bytes after t and assert that the state, codes and predictions at time ≤ t are bit-identical. Assert that calibration prefixes are whole cycles or carry phase causally, that old-cohort training count after the declared transition is zero, and that reads are run on clones only.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E05 (V39 PhaseFront lookahead), V52 phase-alignment leak, E02 (406–431 old presentations after the shift), BYTE_LEARNER v8 non-read-only reads.

skill_recommendations.name: evaluator-population-assertions
skill_recommendations.rule: Derive every evaluator cohort (untouched, revised, noisy, held-out) programmatically from the generator's definitions, with set-algebra unit tests: disjointness, expected sizes, absence from training contexts. Every number reported to the user must carry the arm, trajectory and cohort it was computed from.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E06: V51 'A_untouched' probes were revised plus noisy; V39 max_members came from the wrong arm; the V9.8 single-prefix address diagnostic.

skill_recommendations.name: fixture-quarantine
skill_recommendations.rule: Synthetic or technical fixtures must live under fixtures/, have kind = technical_fixture and a title prefix '[FIXTURE]', use obviously synthetic values, and be excluded from results indexes and summarizer inputs. A summarizer must reject any document whose body declares 'not scientific results'.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E07: FB1 and FB1-followup fixture reports carry the real titles, and one shows the opposite sign.

skill_recommendations.name: guard-power-precheck
skill_recommendations.rule: Before the run, compute each protective guard's expected interval half-width at the planned n. If it cannot detect harm of practically material size (declared in advance), its status is UNASSESSED. Promotion labels then need an explicit owner override, and the reported label must include the guard's power.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E10: FB1's Hoeffding half-width of ±33–38 pp made 'confirmed harm' practically unreachable while candidates were labelled ADVANCE.

skill_recommendations.name: absolute-vs-incremental-decomposition
skill_recommendations.rule: Any claim of protection or retention improvement must report the absolute level, the prechallenge level, the own-state write-minus-no-write difference-in-differences, and a matched-precorrect-item analysis. A change in a relative contrast must be decomposed into its arms before interpretation.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E20: V9.6/V9.7 birth-advantage confounds; the V9.5 rest 'recovery' misread; FB1's absolute first-return ADVANCE.

skill_recommendations.name: unit-fact-registry-check
skill_recommendations.rule: Keep a cross-lineage registry of durable unit facts (claim, scope, evidence path, failure signature), for example 'hash/exact addressing → zero held-out transfer' and '104-dimensional code → residual scale √104'. Each new design must query it for conflicts with its chosen components and state why it expects a different outcome.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E11 (V39 hash fact re-derived in V9.7/V9.8), E22 (104-port scale re-derived in V49), E15 (adopted contrast default failed on a new stream).

skill_recommendations.name: experiment-identity-and-replication
skill_recommendations.rule: Experiment IDs must embed agent, source hash and design hash. Pooling runs that share a version label is forbidden without a declared meta-analysis. 'Independent replication' requires the same locked protocol, a different implementation, and no shared open defects. The runner must assert that the executed source hash equals the design-locked hash, or record a signed amendment.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E14 (V26/V27/V31/V36/V39 collisions), E02 ('independent replication' sharing a buggy stream), E23 (V26 hash mismatch).

skill_recommendations.name: objective-and-next-branch-diff
skill_recommendations.rule: Each design restates the objective verbatim from the canonical contract, and a tool diffs it. Any change, or any departure from a predecessor's preregistered stop or next-branch rule, must cite a dated user instruction or record a rationale for owner approval. Constraints marked core, such as boundedness, cannot stay deferred for more than one round without entering the primary gate.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E21: V47's next branch was ignored and the objective clause changed in V48/V49; boundedness was deferred from V35 to V38 under 'qualified' verdicts.

skill_recommendations.name: closure-claim-scoping
skill_recommendations.rule: Words like 'closed', 'solved', 'exhausted' or 'retired' may only be used with scope tags copied from the source report: representative tested, workload, n, multiplicity status. They need an explicit reopen condition. A closure that contradicts the source report's own caveat is rejected.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E09: the V26 rec's 'storage solved, closed, exhausted' contradicted V23/V24's 'does not eliminate the family'.

skill_recommendations.name: fail-closed-gate-library
skill_recommendations.rule: All gates come from a shared library. Missing, NaN or out-of-range inputs give NOT_EVALUABLE. Zero variance gives NOT_EVALUABLE unless a structural proof is attached. Sign labels require a declared materiality threshold. Coverage checks must equal their denominators. Mutation tests (missing, NaN, impossible values, self-consistent tampering) are run, and an independent replay re-derives the values instead of checking logs only.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E19 (V43 Q7 fail-open, V9.5 validator accepted 2.0 and NaN, log audit accepted self-consistent tampering), E26 (zero-variance rule not kept).

skill_recommendations.name: evidence-level-tagging
skill_recommendations.rule: Every endpoint, figure and summary sentence carries an evidence level E0–E4. Probes that only re-render taught items are E2. Scores from external decoders or engineered heads are tagged EXTERNAL and never counted as learner capability. Promotion toward the core requires E3 with a prior-teaching causal control, delayed and intervening-learning probes, and a result above the strongest shortcut ceiling.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E12, E13 and E27: E1 and E2 evidence drove promotion and 'generalization' narratives, and external decoder scores exceeded native behavior.

skill_recommendations.name: lineage-complete-review
skill_recommendations.rule: When analyzing an archive, group documents by lineage (design → protocol → run → report → audit → erratum → next recommendation) and read the complete chain, whatever era label each member carries. Infer dates from document headers, not version strings.
skill_recommendations.rationale: E25: era labels split design/report/audit pairs and mix chronologies, which reproduces limitation loss at the meta-analysis level.

readers.lens: Era FULL151_TRANSITION_OR_LATER_UPSTREAM of PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023 (19–29 Sep 2026: CORE_RECOVERY A2–A11/BKR/FB1/Post-V5, MATHEMATICAL_INPUT_REVIEW, BYTE_CORE_1/FEAS-1/BYTE_CORE_2, BYTE_LEARNER v3–v8, BYTE_READ_ORDER, BYTE_CORE_V9–V9.10, BYTE_ARITH V1/V2/W3/W4, BYTE→FULL151 bridge steps 1–15, OUTPUT/E3_OUTPUT steps, VISIBLE_CONTEXT/LEARNED_H bridges, stage exit, E3 assay qualification, FE1, THREE_MECHANISM round, R2/Z1 correction, MUSE/REMOTE_13 shared protocols). Focus: incidents, corrections, audit practices, earliest occurrences of recurring failure classes, and durable unit facts.
readers.summary:
Paths are relative to PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023/ unless they start with minifly_b/ or minifly_v3_dev_20261020/. Those are catalog published_paths for documents that already sit in the consolidated tree. 'orig' gives CATALOG sources[0].relative. I read all 162 in-scope documents (85 designs, 77 reports) at least at their decision and limitations sections, and read the incident-bearing ones in full. I also read about 30 documents from the same 19–29 Sep period that the catalog files under EARLY_VERSION or LEGACY because of version-string matching. Several of them are the results or corrections of in-scope designs: the V9.5 audit, V9.6–V9.10 reports, the R2/Z1 E3 correction, the FB1 results and the hostile audits. For context only, I consulted CLAUDE_RECOVERY.md, MINIFLY_OBJECTIVE_CONTRACT.md and ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014. I ran nothing; my only computation was a python extraction from two small SUMMARY.json files.

Main picture. Inside each experiment the work is unusually disciplined: frozen locks, fresh worlds, W/N causal branches, tamper-tested receipt auditors, gates not relaxed after failures, honest E-level labels. Most damage came from four sources:
(1) Small harness and semantic errors that silently disabled a measurement. The change_truth commit-versus-onset defect occurred three times in two days. The 'rel' vs 'relation' branch-ID mismatch made every E3 contrast of the three-mechanism round and the Package B receipts invalid. A2's renamed files gave an empty exclusion set without any error.
(2) Proxy or constructed quantities read as mechanism. Examples: the OMNIBUS10 retention-only endpoint, A6 pooled-mean decompositions, an underpowered 'ideal' decoder, KC distance or decodability standing in for behaviour, and E2 'passes' guaranteed by the candidate's own invariance.
(3) Guards that could not fail: zero-width intervals, a ±38 pp retention-risk band, a materiality δ larger than the whole FULL_151 effect, and a non-functional control printed as '+0.0 [+0.0,+0.0]'.
(4) Lessons that existed locally but were not carried forward. Examples: the sensor losses already measured by READ_ORDER were inherited by the arithmetic line; the zero-variance rule from bridge Steps 6–7 was lost in the three-mechanism round; 'exact addressing kills E3' (V9.8, 26 Sep) was re-derived four more times; the B-birth RNG warning from 19 Sep resurfaced on remote hosts.

The objective itself drifted across consecutive designs: biological front end, then NLP, then four-operation arithmetic evolution, then 1+2=3. The no-backprop constraint was silently relaxed (W3 AdamW/BPTT). The 26 Sep objective contract and the hostile audits caught much of this, and the retrospective says it recurred anyway.

The archive's own era classifier repeats the 18 Sep 'regex over IDs' error. It splits design, result and correction triplets across eras, so any era-scoped review, including this one, misses corrections unless it follows lineage. Durable unit facts:
- FULL_151 is a one-bit valence learner.
- Shared-state writes, not elapsed time, cause the PN-world loss; it is expressed in the slow store.
- FE0 loses byte order beyond the last byte.
- Exact or separated addressing raises taught recall (E1) and abolishes held-out reuse (E3). FE0's shared code gives a reproducible but narrow E3 of about +17–24 pp.
- A rank relation is learnable by a scalar head but a cyclic relation is not.
- B does not transfer from the PN world to bytes.

findings.title: Bookkeeping commit treated as information onset (committed vs delivered truth): earliest recurring scoring defect, three occurrences in two days
findings.description: Doc: A2's frozen exposures_at() counted challenge exposures at/after change_truth, which is 0 for every revised fact because 144 teach events deliver the revised answer before the bookkeeping commit; the reference anchor passed only because in canonical k=1 the flip ordinal equals the probe teach_index ('passed by coincidence'). k=8 revision was 85%/75% under the frozen extractor versus 80.00%/63.75% corrected, and an earlier claim that stratification 'saved 11.25 pp' was withdrawn as the defect itself. The same day, selectivity v1 used the opposite answer at 6/48 anchors: 'the same change_truth-is-a-commit-not-an-onset defect I had already found and fixed in the metrics extractor, reintroduced in a new file'; full-population tracking found the mismatch in 24 windows. On 20 Sep the BKR v5 evaluator again judged anomaly with current scorer truth (truth switches only after all revision teaching), mislabelling scheduled revisions as SINGLE_ANOMALY and leaving CONFIRMED_REVISION empty; 1,536 annotation replays were needed. BYTE_CORE_1 (22 Sep) lists 'committed-vs-delivered truth errors (G1, three occurrences)' from a project audit and scores the delivered byte. A10 adopts challenge-map semantics 'preventing another full annotation-repair replay'. Inference: the fix lived in one module and was not a shared, imported, fixture-tested utility, so each new file re-implemented the naive semantics. An anchor that cannot exercise the edge case (flip==probe) gave false validation.
