findings.generic_safeguard: Re-scoring archived data under a new endpoint set is labeled EXPLORATORY_RESCOPE. It cannot reopen a candidate unless the removed gates are carried as protection endpoints in the confirmation, with the decision rule fixed before the confirmation worlds exist.
findings.recurs_later: The post-hoc reinterpretation pattern recurs in the bridge stage exit (28 Sep) and appears in the post-Full151 retrospective as objective shrink (A01).

findings.title: The owner's stated objective ('ability gained, not blind memorization') was operationalized as an E1 instrument an exact-key table could pass
findings.description: DOCUMENT: BYTE_CORE_1 design (22 Sep): 'Fixed by the project owner ... The instrument measures ... ability gained from relevant experience, not blind memorization.' The route retrospective (A01) states that BYTE-CORE-1's wrapper and revision conditions 'did not exclude a key→consequence memory table', and that 21–26 Sep work shrank to taught-cue retention. The contract was then written on 26 Sep, citing a 'V88–V9.7 objective drift audit'. That audit is not in this archive or the repo. INFERENCE: The proxy (prequential η on taught consequences) replaced the owner's objective inside the very document that recorded it. The retrospective also says the problem recurred after the contract was written.
findings.how_detected: Retrospective objective-drift audit (26 Sep) and route retrospective (14 Oct), both re-reading the designs
findings.generic_safeguard: Every design states its E-level and runs the recitation countermodel (exact-key, canonical-key, frequency) against the primary gate before the design is frozen. If the countermodel can pass, the design must say the claim is E1/E2.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A01: it recurred after the 26 Sep contract. The post-Full151 'taught exact recall is secondary' critique (Oct 13) shows it still needed restating.

findings.title: A proxy measured in the wrong state vetoed a front end; a prior interface verdict was ignored, and 3,072 confirmation lives ran on a floor-level interface
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Claude's FEAS draft (23 Sep) lists its own S0–S1 errors: no feasibility or futility gate before confirmation ('3,072 confirmation lives on a floor-level interface'); 'Front end chosen by a geometry proxy measured after a 7-day rest (E11)', when FE1's habituation had decayed to about 0, so the proxy vetoed FE1; 'Offset seen in smoke tests (A9), but the decoder was left bias-free', because 'I also declared engineering smoke results off-limits for design changes'; verdicts issued at the floor (CLOCK_INSENSITIVE). And: 'V52 had already shown that the interface binds for V50 ... The right design would have made the front-end screen the first block.' INFERENCE: A lesson recorded on 12 Sep (V52 NO_DEPLOYABLE_INTERFACE_CANDIDATE) did not reach the 22 Sep design. A well-meant anti-tuning rule blocked the fix of a defect that was known before launch.
findings.how_detected: Implementer's own post-hoc erratum, explicitly labeled POST HOC (ERRATUM_SUMMARY.json)
findings.generic_safeguard: Run a futility or feasibility screen with a positive control before any confirmation. Measure a proxy only in the state the learner actually operates in. Smoke results may change implementation and decoder definitions (not science thresholds) through a logged amendment. Earlier verdicts on the same interface are mandatory preconditions in the design's evidence table.
findings.recurs_later: BYTE_ARITH V2 (26 Sep) reused the 1 s byte clock and 128-bin pooling that BYTE_READ_ORDER (25 Sep) had already shown to lose order and collapse the native arm (F14).

findings.title: Leakage and shortcut paths inflated a reported milestone (cross-record cue), and a generator exploit was flagged earlier
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Earliest: the V26 report (7 Sep) labels a salience candidate 'task_specific_salience_exploit' that 'won only because the generator gives the informative coordinate 2.17x the nuisance variance'. BYTE_CORE_1 (22 Sep) published V50-REF F1 η = 0.4616. The erratum and FEAS later show that 'window learners on 8-byte records read the previous record's consequence': first-presentation AUC 0.759, where nothing cue-specific can yet be known. FEAS v3 also found that FE-NI's read() updated long-term state, giving 'a per-record sampling pulse'. The fix was a consequence-decoupled control, a leaky XR fixture and day-probe checks. INFERENCE: In a byte stream, any integrator whose window spans record boundaries is a leak by default.
evidence: results/39b82f8edd724356_ERRATUM_SUMMARY.json (orig: BYTE_CORE_1_ERRATUM_20260923/ERRATUM_SUMMARY.json) — 'POST HOC', T7 xrecord detector fires on V50 F1
findings.how_detected: Post-hoc erratum re-analysis with a designed leak detector (first-presentation AUC) and a review of the v2 interface contract
findings.generic_safeguard: Leak battery before science: first-presentation AUC (must be at chance), a consequence-decoupled run, a planted-leak fixture that must be detected, and a requirement that read() is pure.
findings.recurs_later: Shortcut-passable gates in BYTE_ARITH (F13). The 'one-bit class rule can solve it' caveat is attached to every later E3 assay.

findings.title: A shortcut countermodel passed the main gate; marginal gates passed lives that failed half the task; a 'sealed' set was used for design decisions (BYTE_ARITH warmup)
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Hostile audit (26 Sep): a 'deliberately weak countermodel' (stored answers, reversed operands, operator mode) scores 19.0% vs 7.7% exact, a +11.2-point gain, passing the Stage-1 +10-point gate. The '128 sealed' questions are used to decide representation changes, so 'they become development evidence', and the universe is finite (840 expressions). Two '0…−5' grade functions with different bands coexist (V1 vs V2). The second audit: a score matrix where each life gets 32/32 on two operators and 0/32 on two passes every marginal condition, yet no life handles all four. The answer stream can be 'decorative' because targets bypass the sensory path. Both audits build explicit counterexamples with small computations.
evidence: results/d839dc4c3e33f97c_REPORT.md (orig: BYTE_ARITH_WARMUP_REAUDIT_20260926/REPORT.md) — marginal vs joint gate; decorative answer stream
findings.how_detected: Hostile audit that constructs adversarial countermodels and score matrices, executed as small deterministic calculations
findings.generic_safeguard: Each gate must fail against a fixed countermodel battery (lookup, symmetry, mode/frequency, constant, one-bit class). Use joint per-unit floors instead of marginal medians. Any set consulted for a design decision is reclassified as development. Single-import grading functions with boundary tests.
findings.recurs_later: Codified in the E0–E4 contract (26 Sep). Post-Full151 designs still need explicit shortcut-superiority additions (arithmetic_feedback_rule_discovery_dev_v2_20261013/design/EXPERIMENT.md:153).

findings.title: Program-level drift: an evolution search whose best success would not advance the goal, run on an interface with already-measured losses
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Claude's program hostile audit (26 Sep): 'Even full success does not advance the stated goal': all Full151 native plasticity frozen, an engineered decoder trained with AdamW, one searched route with 'no fly component at all'. Gates sit 3–7× above what fully supervised training reached (supervised GRU 5.5–10.9% exact with 512 answers vs gate 37.5%/50%). The V2 sensor uses a 1 s byte clock and 128-bin pooling, both measured as lossy in BYTE_READ_ORDER. The preflight report: V2 evolution evaluated 131,072 candidates, 'did not form a continuous 128-generation lineage' (325 family extinctions with reseeding), and learned 1.3% vs a no-write arm at 7.7%. INFERENCE: An expensive search went ahead without a privileged positive control or an attribution check against the native core. This prefigures retrospective nodes A03/A04/A07.
evidence: results/9b9736c166bf5550_REPORT.md (orig: BYTE_ARITH_WARMUP_PREFLIGHT_20260926/REPORT.md) — V2 table and lineage extinctions
results/c69e155a7baa1dcf_REPORT.md, results/2fb597f44858e907_REPORT.md (orig: BYTE_READ_ORDER_FLYROUTE_20260925/, BYTE_READ_ORDER_ITER2_20260925/) — FE0 order loss, LAT4 passes
findings.how_detected: Re-reading designs against the objective contract plus quantitative comparison with existing results (no new runs)
findings.generic_safeguard: Before any search: (1) a privileged learner must reach the gate on development data; (2) the design names which native component will receive credit and includes a route ablation; (3) the design imports measured interface limits.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A03/A04/A07/A08 (October): engineered learners and new substrates attributed to 'MiniFly'.

findings.title: Capabilities of different systems or tasks merged under one 'core' label
findings.description: DOCUMENT: V50 verdict FUNCTIONAL_CORE_ESTABLISHED (11 Sep, CUE8 task, G0–G9 pass). The next day, V51 BYTE256 shows A held-out 0.02 and D 0.42. The V68 review (13 Sep) warns that the label 'is not evidence that MiniFly recovered a fly core'. The bridge stage-exit decision (28 Sep) separates CONTENT E1 (four answer stores, 512/512) from FE0 E3 (single valence store plus a binary comparator, +17.2 pts): 'the two sets of results cannot be added and called one verified fly brain'. It also notes that the post-hoc FE0+0.02×CONTENT weight is not confirmation. INFERENCE: The risk was identified twice before Full151, yet the route retrospective (A02, A03, A06, A07) shows it recurred repeatedly in October.
findings.how_detected: Later reviews re-reading scope (V68 review, stage-exit decision)
findings.generic_safeguard: Verdict labels must include task, interface and substrate (e.g. CUE8_ASSOC_CORE_AT_LOAD128). A capability claim for system X requires one frozen configuration of X passing all named tasks in the same trial. Keep an inheritance ledger: mother learner, preserved state, write/read/feedback paths.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A02/A03/A06/A07 (7–14 Oct).

findings.title: Summaries and catalogs dropped preregistered verdicts and limitations (the retrospective's core failure, visible before Full151)
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Catalog independent audit (28 Sep): the mechanism catalog quotes correct percentages but omits preregistered failures. PAIR is 90.04% overall but its per-cue gate failed (weakest cue 12/32). LAT4's 0.93–0.98 KC decoding came from a post-hoc refit, while the preregistered decoder gate failed. 'READY' meant source exists, not qualified on the current platform. The program description was stale. A6 audit (20 Sep): the chat memo's quoted values had the sign of 'native minus mean-subtracted', so 'they are not centering gains', and the K=8 decomposition 'differs fundamentally from the K=2 example emphasized'. INFERENCE: Limitations were usually right in local reports and got lost in handoff layers (memos, catalogs, recommendations).
evidence: results/58d362442643b7ea_REPORT.md (orig: PROJECT_AUDIT_A6_20260920/REPORT.md) — 'Two further corrections to the memo'
PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014/REPORT.md — '限制进入下一轮设计和口头总结时没有被持续保留'
findings.how_detected: Independent read-only audit of handoff documents against the original reports and receipts
findings.generic_safeguard: Any summary row that quotes a number must quote the preregistered verdict and E-level next to it, pulled from a machine-readable decision file. Summaries are generated, not hand-written, from DECISION.json and status vectors.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective (14 Oct) identifies this as the central recurring failure.

findings.title: Selective endpoint display: a shortlist hid a +9.6 pp endpoint and a −1.1 pp trade-off
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A2 timecourse decision (19 Sep): 'I displayed a five-endpoint extractor shortlist and omitted P2, P3 and P7.' Recomputed from the same saved cells: P7 +9.64 [+4.99,+14.28] (0/8 blocks negative), P2 −1.08 [−1.85,−0.31]. 'Nothing reaches 5 pp' and 'No trade-off' are both withdrawn. The primary P1 'is not re-chosen after seeing P7'. INFERENCE: The omission went in both directions (a hidden benefit and a hidden cost), so it is a reporting-process fault, not motivated selection. A reviewer still had to catch it.
findings.how_detected: External reviewer pointed to saved-but-unreported endpoints; offline recomputation
findings.generic_safeguard: The report generator prints every saved endpoint with interval and status. Any shortlist must list the omitted endpoints by name. Primary-endpoint immutability is checked against the protocol hash.
findings.recurs_later: Same family as F16.

findings.title: Metrics, gates and 'findings' true by construction (tautologies)
findings.description: DOCUMENT: V52 refinement (12 Sep): the stationarity gate on target-context self-overlap 'is ~1.0 by construction and gates nothing'. A2 (19 Sep): 'Additivity residual is 0.000 pp in every cell (denominators match by construction)', later relabeled as 'an algebraic identity and a zero additivity residual identifies nothing'. A6 audit (20 Sep): linear M transfer is rank ≤1 'by construction'. A10 review (20 Sep): 'I is defined by subtraction, then its closure is used as validation'. FB1 audits (21 Sep): A_WR=1 under a fixed dictionary is a structural identity, and nested-partition collisions are necessarily monotone. BYTE_CORE_1 (22 Sep): E-2a 'structural zero ... clock scaling cannot act', yet a CLOCK_INSENSITIVE verdict was issued.
findings.how_detected: Refinement audits and hostile audits doing algebra on the definitions
findings.generic_safeguard: For each gate or metric, the designer writes 'how could this fail?' and ships a fixture where it does fail. Structural identities are reported as implementation checks, never as results.
findings.recurs_later: Post-Full151: rest intervals that are 'a parameter no-op' (native_interface_transfer_dev_v1_20261015/REPORT.md:43; arithmetic_feedback_rule_discovery_design_v2_20261013/EXPERIMENT.md:113), and retrospective A07 '24小时只推进时钟的稳定'.

findings.title: A durable harness limit (encode-once, so no changed-presentation data) was rediscovered at least four times
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A2 (19 Sep §5): evaluate_life encodes codes once, so input-side rewiring 'may never reach the input representation'. FB1 v2 audit (21 Sep): 'There is no defined same identity, different rendering data', so A_WR=1 is structural. Minimal-core v2 audit (21 Sep): dynamic input plasticity would yield false negatives. A11 characterization audit (21 Sep): the panel inherited a 32-active-PN spec from another model line on the same fixed-cue interface. Bridge stage exit (28 Sep): the E2 variants 'map to the same effective four-byte key — narrow E2'. INFERENCE: A unit fact central to the E2/E3 ladder (the harness cannot even present changed renderings) was never recorded as a standing harness-capability note, so every new design re-paid for it.
findings.how_detected: Each time by a reviewer reading runner source lines (v88 runner :731 etc.)
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a HARNESS_CAPABILITIES.md (what the evaluator can and cannot present, cache semantics, clocks), hashed and required reading. Every design declares which capabilities it relies on.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A07/A09: interface changes later created new substrates, partly because the old harness could not express the new tasks.

findings.title: Wrong constants, cost premises and stale state used to justify design scope (and auditors' own errors)
findings.description: DOCUMENT: FB1 v2 audit (21 Sep): stable-window absolute times hard-coded from the regular task were wrong for high-load (5,685,120 vs 1,693,440 s); historical SD quoted as 7.759 vs 7.402 recomputed; runtime taken from a report-generation elapsed time (about 5 s); a replay budget with the arithmetic error 8×2 = 16 stated as fitting under 8. A11 v2 audit (25 Sep): the scope cut rested on a cost premise that receipts contradict (full grid 19–23 CPU-h, under the cap). The A11 v2.1 review then corrects the audit itself: its 'B at 1.7× slower' 'was in the wrong direction', and cost was not the user's reason. The A9 design audit (20 Sep): the proposal 'A9 one-shot v3' required sealing an E2 that had already been opened. INFERENCE: Audits also err. The two-sided review loop (design → audit → response → re-review) caught auditor errors too.
findings.how_detected: Audit recomputation from receipts and resource ledgers, and the response round that checked the audit
findings.generic_safeguard: Constants and costs must be cited to a receipt or ledger row with a hash. Audits get one rebuttal round and their own errata. Every design checks 'already done?' against the current state pointer.
findings.recurs_later: Post-Full151: header comments still drift from actual tensors (minifly_recoverability_v1_r2_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:55, 5,801 vs 5,537).

findings.title: Silent empty sets and coverage holes in exclusion and stratification
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A2 follow-up (19 Sep): inherited worlds had been renamed, so the exclusion glob matched nothing and the set was 'silently empty'. The fix was a guard that aborts if inherited worlds contribute zero cues. FB1 v2 audit (21 Sep): the historical exclusion scanner searched only one root and missed A10 worlds stored in another. V9.5 refinement (25 Sep): an exploratory split was empty because 'every old pair contains a shared symbol'.
findings.how_detected: The implementer's own pre-use check (A2), a hostile audit reading the scan paths (FB1), and a refinement audit (V9.5)
findings.generic_safeguard: Assert nonzero, expected-magnitude counts for every exclusion set, stratum and population. Keep a cross-root world/seed registry. Empty splits fail closed.
findings.recurs_later: Same family as F04.

findings.title: Engineering fixtures produced science-shaped reports with opposite or identical verdicts (label-confusion risk)
findings.description: DOCUMENT: V88 engineering_evidence/parallel/round_A/REPORT.md reports 'Status: TRACE_RESTORATION_NOT_CONFIRMED' from a 2-history fixture. The file has no fixture disclaimer (the disclaimer is in TEST_REPORT.md), while the native Round A on 48 histories 'passed'. The FB1 qualification-pipeline FINAL_DECISION.md ('TECHNICAL SYNTHETIC FIXTURE') carries a status table identical to the real FINAL_DECISION.md. INFERENCE: An archive scan or summarizer reading REPORT/FINAL_DECISION filenames can invert or fabricate verdicts.
findings.how_detected: Inferred in this audit by comparing files; not flagged in the originals
findings.generic_safeguard: Fixture outputs carry evidence_class=FIXTURE in machine-readable headers and filenames (FIXTURE_REPORT.md). Summarizers and publishers refuse to treat them as verdicts.
findings.recurs_later: Unknown post-Full151. The risk grows with automated archive summarization.

findings.title: 'Validated' without native execution; reviews claimed reruns that could not be verified
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Iteration 8 (13 Sep): 'I found neither Claude's scripts/DoOR input files nor the chat review's claimed rerun records in the project ... that does not verify its claimed independent execution'. Independent recomputation also found a likely units error (signed synapse count × 0.275) behind the signature claims, and the 647-KC learning-equivalence claim remained unverified. Iteration 10 later found none of the 12 compression families passed and the 647-KC example 'unaccepted'. The V83 back-test (15 Sep): 'The earlier V83 runner was not shipped again after only syntax checking.' V86/V87 QA: the ChatGPT sandbox lacked the backend, so only 'non-scientific deterministic mock integration' ran.
findings.how_detected: Independent recomputation from the source graph (iteration 8); staged back-tests (V83)
findings.generic_safeguard: QA claims carry an execution level (STATIC / MOCK / NATIVE_SMOKE / NATIVE_FULL). A claimed rerun needs a receipt hash in the repo. Nothing ships to the owner's machine without a native smoke test.
findings.recurs_later: Claude A V3 (29–30 Sep): Muse's source, locks and receipts were unavailable, so Package A was reimplemented rather than audited.

findings.title: Lost design specs and provenance gaps forced re-specification
findings.description: DOCUMENT: V41/V42 (about 10 Sep): 'The complete numerical protocol was unavailable', so the design was rebuilt from 'latest recoverable chat recommendations' and labeled as refinements. V88: 'V87 runner source absent from result archive'. A6: K=2 captures lack per-event source rows. Claude A V3: Muse's files unavailable. The archive README: some artifacts were 'permanently unlinked' by an earlier cleanup, and macOS refused access to Trash (records moved there on 21 Sep).
findings.how_detected: Discovered when the next agent tried to reproduce or extend
findings.generic_safeguard: Commit every design (including chat-derived ones), runner source and receipts to the repo with hashes before execution. Destructive cleanup needs a manifest and a reviewer.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective cites sources under DIGITALBABY_CLAUDE_B_* copies; consolidated publication on 23 Oct was itself a recovery effort.

findings.title: Operational errors forced re-simulation or produced invalid fields
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A2 ran 'two pilot instances concurrently into one output directory'. The first pilot 'stored only summaries, so the scoring fix forced a full re-simulation'. SHA256SUMS hashed itself. R2/Z1 v1.1: the nested world directory did not exist, so zero receipts were committed, and the analysis crashed on a scope error after the summary was written. Step 1 v2: JSON-list vs tuple source-check bug. Persistence auditor: numpy.bool_ JSON failure. Step 11: code did not save old-end held-out scores although the prose required them. BYTE→FULL151: predictor_total_variation computed with the intact distribution in both arms, so it was zero and invalid. Selectivity v1: '--resume parsed, never read'. INFERENCE: Each failure was small, but they repeatedly turned into confusion or recomputation. They were handled honestly: no receipts overwritten, disclosed amendments.
findings.how_detected: Runtime failures, interleaved outputs, and audit of output fields against the design
findings.generic_safeguard: Single-writer lockfiles. Persist raw receipts sufficient for offline rescoring. Run the full report and packaging pipeline on a technical world (outputs checked against the design's output list) before science. Unit-test every CLI flag.
findings.recurs_later: Post-Full151 still discloses incomplete closure locks and missing checkpoints (minifly_recoverability_v1_r2_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:53).

findings.title: Numerics and sign errors in objectives, surrogates and statistics
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A2: 'a hand-rolled incomplete beta was wrong by up to 4× at df = 15 earlier in this project', so the code now refuses to approximate. A delete-one-world jackknife was mislabeled as a world-aware SE. Selectivity v1: an objective sign error 'rewarded coordinates that damage protected facts', caught before reporting. A surrogate coefficient was '113.1× off'. V43 PROTOCOL_ERRATUM, before execution: a sentence in an adopted independent review claiming capture could exceed 1 was mathematically wrong. A6: a Rayleigh-ratio objective proposal 'rewards a large wrong-sign self effect'.
findings.how_detected: Self-check before reporting; external audit; pre-science erratum
findings.generic_safeguard: Use library statistics only. Sign-check fixtures for every objective, where a planted harmful update must score worse. Dimensional and units checks on surrogates.
findings.recurs_later: Not obviously after 26 Sep in this archive.

findings.title: Known-failed families and known liabilities re-entered new designs
findings.description: DOCUMENT: V68 review (13 Sep): 'V48 already tested a global APL-like controller ... failed ... Another gain sweep of that abstraction would repeat old work.' It also lists deferred items, e.g. 'another 647-KC compression claim'. The FEAS erratum (23 Sep) found FE1 habituation 'carries a multi-day retention cost'. The FE1 single-mechanism case (28 Sep) then failed its anti-regression gate: final taught-relation W 26.95 pp below FE0, and E3 θ −9.64. BYTE_ARITH reused known interface losses (F14). INFERENCE: The ledger of failed or limited mechanisms existed (later the 50+ pruned summary, 26 Sep) but was not enforced as a design precondition.
evidence: designs/47e54dcf404ec57d_DESIGN_v4.md (orig: BYTE_CORE_FEAS_1_20260923/DESIGN_v4.md) — FE1-NI dropped for retention cost
findings.how_detected: Review reading project history (V68); outcome of a frozen test (FE1)
findings.generic_safeguard: Each design includes a 'prior evidence on this exact variant' table drawn from the mechanism ledger, with explicit justification if a known liability is retested.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A10: mechanism ID mismatches across 108/136/254/71/16-item views.

findings.title: Audit independence mattered: log-consistency and shared-helper audits missed faults that replay audits caught
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Claude A V3 launch review (30 Sep): 'a self-consistent joint change of Z2's gated amount, target and bucket is accepted by the log audit and rejected by the replay'. Z2_rand was not truly yoked: +5.07% dose mismatch, fixed to an exact yoke. V9.5: 'implementer-audited, not independently audited' was disclosed (A3), and the later independent reducer found validator defects. Three-mechanism: the auditor used the runner's branch helper (F01). V42 final audit, which recomputed all 12,000 probe rows independently, passed without change. INFERENCE: Assurance scales with independence: re-reading < recompute from receipts < separate-implementation replay with tamper battery.
findings.how_detected: Replay re-implementation plus a tamper battery that included jointly consistent corruptions
findings.generic_safeguard: Every audit declares its level: L0 read, L1 recompute from receipts with separate code, L2 replay with an independent implementation not importing the runner, L3 adversarial tamper battery including self-consistent joint tampering. Promotion requires L2 or higher.
findings.recurs_later: Post-Full151 studies adopt independent replay and acceptance cycles (studies/rcenter-survivor-rounds-20261003/audits/).

findings.title: Overloaded identifiers: version names, E-labels, 'FULL_151', 'B' and mechanism IDs meant different things
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Two different 'V39' experiments existed: ChatGPT's preregistered 'Earned Consolidation' (TRACE-CORR, 8 seeds) and Claude's 'bounded superposed memory' (26 cells × 16 seeds). A8/A9 used E1/E2/E3 for development, sealed confirmation and shuffle phases, unrelated to the later E0–E4 evidence ladder. The A6 audit: 'FULL_151 is a candidate identifier, not 151 neurons'. The minimal-core audit: the budget symbol B collided with module B. 'V52' exists in two folders with different designs. INFERENCE: Name collisions make cross-version summaries silently wrong. The route retrospective's A10 (U042/U034/U055 mismatches) is the later form.
evidence: results/589de53c61e50eb3_SUMMARY.md vs results/4756a22b788096ab_SUMMARY.md (orig: V51_Mac_M3/v52_claude/ vs V52_Mac_M3/v52_results/)
findings.how_detected: Audits noticing the ambiguity, plus this comparison
findings.generic_safeguard: Use globally unique experiment IDs (agent, date, slug) and a registry. Reserved vocabulary (E0–E4, core, adopted) with fixed meanings. Mechanism identity = source ID + equation version + substrate + task contract.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A10 (October).

findings.title: Protocols grew into long specifications with unreachable or contradictory decision states
findings.description: DOCUMENT: A11 v3.8 (23 Sep, about 80 KB) is 'a narrow implementation-readiness erratum' that 'makes the TRIAGE_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE A-only path reachable'. Minimal-core v2 (21 Sep): 'the selector rule references experimental results that do not exist' (G*+H* first appears in Campaign II), a compression stage 'hid a new learning mechanism', and PROGRAM_FINISHED was conflated with success. FEAS went through seven versions on 23 Sep. v6.1 had to add a state table because non-confirmation paths had no defined outputs. INFERENCE: Iterative hostile review improved rigor but also bred complexity, which created new defects and delayed science. The user later asked for 'one-hour' smaller questions.
evidence: designs/f1c9888ad1fbb00d_A11_MODULAR_A_REDESIGN_V2_1_REVIEW_20260925.md C2 — user asked for smaller questions
findings.how_detected: Readiness audits enumerating reachable states and data dependencies
findings.generic_safeguard: Represent decision rules as executable state machines with exhaustive-path tests (every terminal state reachable, every quantity defined). Cap protocol size and push complexity into code with tests.
findings.recurs_later: Post-Full151 design cycles report 'three-cycle' reviews closing ledger gaps (arithmetic_two_designs_20261013/THREE_CYCLE_REVIEW.md).

findings.title: Positive generalization evidence was not carried forward; the retrospective had to reassert it
findings.description: DOCUMENT: Before Full151, native REF showed limited E3 on never-reinforced combinations: V9.9A +17.19 [+10.39,+23.98], V9.9B +9.57. V9.10C showed an online 5,177-weight shared head reached 77.54% on never-reinforced rank comparisons (+27.54 pp teaching effect) and retained 75.39% after a day and a new cohort. Z0 showed W−N +38.0 (F01). The route retrospective (14 Oct) has to state that 'Full151 is not never-generalizing' and that this 'suffices to reject the generalization that all old cores can only do exact lookup'. INFERENCE: Positive unit facts were lost as much as limitations were. Later work rebuilt arithmetic on new substrates without an explicit comparison to these native E3 baselines.
findings.how_detected: Retrospective re-reading the history
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a standing 'capability baselines' table (task family, E-level, effect, substrate, receipt). Every new core must be compared to it on the same assay, or state explicitly why it can't be.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A03/A06/A09 (October).

findings.title: Adoption or recommendation labels emitted without a demonstrated benefit
findings.description: DOCUMENT: The V51 design rule: ELIG-WRITE 'is eligible for default adoption only if fresh evidence shows a useful benefit'. The V51 SUMMARY shows CUE8 load-128 A_final_heldout identical for V50-REF and ELIG-WRITE (0.80078125 vs 0.80078125), D_final 0.9805 vs 0.9824, and ELIG-WRITE worse on BYTE256 D_final (0.21 vs 0.42). Yet the output is 'Configuration recommendation: ADOPT_ELIG_WITHIN_CUE128'. INFERENCE (PLAUSIBLE; the full decision table is not in the archive): an automated recommendation string appears to have been emitted without the required benefit. This is the earliest form of 'adoption without confirmation'.
findings.how_detected: Inferred here by comparing the decision string with the reported numbers and the design rule
findings.generic_safeguard: Adoption strings are produced only by a tested decision function that prints the exact rule and per-condition statuses. 'User-adopted development baseline' is a separate label from 'scientifically confirmed'.
findings.recurs_later: Route retrospective A06: COV-SUPPORT adopted with NO_ADVANCE_RETAIN_COV_R, no independent confirmation, 0 confirmation worlds (addition_core_v2_support_v1_20261011/ADOPTION.json).

unit_facts: V20 (6 Sep; results/67d35b7d1fa5f061_v20_results_review.md <- v20_results_review.md): an output-column gain controller on a normalized delta rule cannot change the overlap factor a^T h. It therefore cannot selectively protect overlapping old associations. Exact, shuffled and feedback-disabled arms had identical endpoints (A after B 49.54%, ridge 98.61%).

V28 (7 Sep; designs/9a09a44b5e7f7c29_v28_experiment_recommendation.md): a valid retention or compatibility task needs four things: recall of the same trained identities (not fresh latent pairs), arbitrary bindings, measured headroom at the encoder quality actually used, and no replay. Otherwise a 'Pareto' verdict measures rule generalization.

V39/V40 (9 Sep; designs/bf66d97e7165c883_v40_experiment_recommendation.md): a bounded superposed store generalizes one-shot (E1 held-out 0.998) but collapses with load (wall 0.936 at load 32, 0.092 at 256). Admission-controlled slots bound storage 11.3× but cannot generalize before binding. Code stationarity dominated separation ratio: a phase normalizer that keeps updating drifts 62% of the active units.

V42 (results/61bea9b3dc0f80dd_v42_analysis_report.md): lower log loss coincided with 92 fewer correct next-byte predictions. bpb and accuracy are not interchangeable, and the E1 held-out endpoint was saturated (512/512 for all policies).

V43 (results/d7d7cdefe31c1cc3_v43_analysis_report.md): old held-out recall stayed about 99% while new-cohort acquisition collapsed (load 256: 1/16 valid; load 512: 0/16). Old-memory probes alone do not show continued learning. Only 0.41% of arbitration events were identity targets, so the training population differed from the evaluation population.

V52-Claude (12 Sep; results/589de53c61e50eb3_SUMMARY.md <- V51_Mac_M3/v52_claude): in the V51-LAG byte line, writing at every byte destroys usable memory (A after D 0.031). Target-only writing gives 0.23, and position-random writes 0.008. On BYTE256, whole-stream averages are dominated by framing bytes (framing acc 0.967 vs whole 0.531; results/c88df11ee721c9d3_BYTE_CLASS_METRICS.csv).

MiniFly V66 (13 Sep; results/30032ad45886007e_REPORT.md <- minifly/REPORT.md): same-cue, magnitude-matched consequence swaps change the next-day effect on an old memory from −0.443 to +0.501 Hz. The direction and local expression of the actual writes explain signed interference.

Physiology source audit (13 Sep; results/fe1bf4999541ade5_REPORT.md): 12 of 60 observations used in the reduced fit differ from the final published Huang 2024 data. The α3→DAN gain sits at about −19.99 log, next to its initialization of −20, so it may be unidentified.

A2 target-slot / localization (19 Sep; results/86a1793ee7e8bed9_A2_FOLLOWUP_REPORT_20260919.md, results/a68efbbadeeae6f8_NEXT_STEP_DECISION.md): sharing state with other cohorts' learning costs 15–24 pp with target timing held identical. A 3.4× stretch of the schedule costs about 0. An aged learner acquires a fresh cohort 7.44 pp better. The slow state carries 23.70 of the 24.13 pp rescue.

A2 interventions (19 Sep; results/97dae9219f3aebb5_NEXT_STEP_DECISION.md, results/ce115f1815deebad_DECISION.md): re-routing deposition between fast and slow under a conserved alpha budget cut slow L1 by 32% but moved P1 by only +0.24 pp. It trades first-return accuracy (−2.86 pp) for reacquisition after 4 exposures (+9.64 pp). Lower norm with unchanged performance is not success.

A2 selectivity v2 (19 Sep; results/618535acd0e9de8e_V2_DECISION.md, results/c12f349d57bbe2e0_WRITE_SELECTIVITY_REPORT.md): a constrained oracle allocation gives +5.6 to +6.8 pp on protected facts with a net incoming gain. Selectivity is a bout-scale, not event-scale, property (one event touches 47 of 5177 coordinates). The needed signal (other facts' readout dependence) is not a function of the coordinate's own local state: a structural observability gap.

A6/A7 (20 Sep; results/58d362442643b7ea_REPORT.md, results/aef31ebacea60182_REPORT.md): cross-block mean subtraction (LOBO) gives +6.12 pp active accuracy at K=8, with 1,295 wrong→correct and 731 correct→wrong decisions. It is diagnostic headroom with real tail harm, not harmless denoising, and same-block subtraction gives −23.58 pp.

BKR V5 (20–21 Sep; results/4cd35860ea6df529_REPORT.md): B beats REF on 16 of 19 endpoints (K8 current usefulness +5.50 pp), but K8 first return is still only 50.85%. Adding K or R gives no incremental benefit or confirmed trade-offs. Reactivation gains after reteaching (+9.34 pp) must not be counted as retention, since first return drops (−7.13 pp K8).
FB1 follow-up (22 Sep; results/428a50a89005dc77_REPORT.md): at 8 partitions, fixed hash routing beats geometric routing (geometric−hash −6.02 [−7.69,−4.36] pp).

BYTE_CORE_1 / FEAS (22–23 Sep; results/0430791c95445acb_INSPECTION_REPORT.md, results/b13609d33b21ae61_REPORT.md): FULL_151 with the FE0 byte front end learns near the floor (η 0.0047 vs FE-ID oracle 0.2557). FE0's codes carry more information than FULL_151 uses (online NLMS η 0.079), and a learned common offset depresses the frozen decoder. Final-7-day η was negative for every front end.

BYTE_READ_ORDER (25 Sep; results/c69e155a7baa1dcf_REPORT.md, results/2fb597f44858e907_REPORT.md): the FE0 input organ keeps the latest byte but loses the one before (0.22 decodability). 128-bin pooling collapses the native arm. An order-preserving LAT4 feeding all 5,177 KCs passed the V9 ORDER gate in 3 of 3 worlds.

V9.4/V9.5 (25–26 Sep; results/6e102459eefc8a38_REPORT.md, results/6a9f765adc858339_AUDIT_REPORT.md): four successfully learned new byte cohorts cause a persistent −11.33 pp old-choice cost at +24 h (123/563 old pairs lost vs 3 without writes). The narrowing of the contrast after rest comes from the no-write arm losing its temporary advantage, not from recovery.

V9.7 (results/008d8788aee0284b_REPORT.md): HASH8 raises absolute old and new choice but doubles the write-induced old-memory penalty (−22.14 vs −10.94; DID −11.20). Separated stores start stronger and lose more.

V9.8–V9.9 (26 Sep; results/8ad93977a33314a9_REPORT.md, results/dc06f516f2f5bae2_REPORT.md, minifly_b/package/DOCS/BYTE_CORE_V9_9A/REPORT.md): native REF shows causal E3 on never-reinforced combinations (V9.9A +17.19 pp, V9.9B rank +9.57 pp). HASH8 keeps taught pairs but loses that transfer. Doubling early writes adds only +2.34 pp.

V9.10A–E (26–27 Sep; results/711351597327d471_REPORT.md, results/cfe49b4f76eb5442_REPORT.md, results/7237c8e92dc9bcb8_REPORT.md, results/79eb1e61f8099fb4_REPORT.md): native taught-edge margins contain relational information that external aggregation extracts (76.17% vs 60.74% direct). An online shared 5,177-weight KC head reaches 77.54% held-out rank with retention 75.39% after a day and a new cohort. The same head fails cyclic relations (51.0%, bounded at 6/9 for a scalar per symbol). That failure is not a zero-overlap obstruction.

BYTE_ARITH (26 Sep; results/9b9736c166bf5550_REPORT.md): a supervised raw-byte GRU with 512 answers reaches only 5.5–10.9% exact on unseen one-operator expressions, with MAE about 4. V2 evolution reached 1.3% learned vs 7.7% no-write on novel expressions.

Full151 bridge (27–28 Sep; minifly_b/package/DOCS/BYTE_FULL151_BRIDGE_STAGE_EXIT_DECISION_20260928.md): the CONTENT 4-byte-key route gives E1 512/512 and 99.22% old recall after four new batches (a −0.78 pp measurable loss). Its E2 variants map to the same effective key (narrow E2). FE0 E3 is +17.2 pp on a different single-store task, while CONTENT on that task is −1.0 pp.

R2/Z1 correction (29 Sep; results/994af59f25e9acb0_REPORT.md): with a working prior-teaching control, native Z0 gives W−N +38.0 pp on six never-reinforced old relation orientations after a day, an intervening cohort and another day. The Z1 eligibility split is worse (−14.6 pp).

Harness constraint (19–21 Sep; results/07e62861f41ae86c_REPORT.md §3): the V88 evaluate_life encodes world['pn'] once per life. It has no changed-rendering data, so E2 cannot be tested and dynamic input plasticity is invisible unless the encoding path is replaced.
process_observations:
Review practices that actually changed verdicts or claims were the ones that re-executed or recomputed:
- V39 gate re-analysis of saved trajectories (verdict flipped no_capacity_pressure→qualified)
- the ChatGPT scoring audit of A2 with independent replay (revision denominators, n=64 plan voided, 3 claims withdrawn)
- the selectivity v1 audit (6 findings; v2 verdict reworded with individual losses)
- iteration-8 recomputation from the FlyWire graph (units error; 647-KC claim unverified, later rejected in iteration 10)
- the A6 recomputation from NPZ with a separate implementation (gain real, explanation revised)
- the BKR V5 annotation replay (bitwise-identical states, mechanism tables replaced)
- the V9.5 independent reducer (validator defects, rest interpretation corrected)
- the R2/Z1 literal-branch auditor (prior E3 contrasts invalidated)
- the Claude A V3 replay audit (caught a self-consistent tamper that the log audit accepted)

Re-reading or hostile design audits mostly changed designs or stopped programs before science rather than flipping results:
- FEAS v1→v6.1: seven versions in one day, many semantic fixes
- FB1 v2→v3.1: ~8 high findings
- minimal-core v2 (P1 list)
- BYTE_ARITH: two NO-GO audits plus Claude's program-level NO-GO
- V43's pre-freeze review (a fail-open gate fixed before data)

These were cheap and high-yield, especially when the auditor read the actual runner lines and built counterexamples.

Review failure modes:
- the auditor imported runner helpers (three-mechanism, F01)
- log-only consistency audits (Claude A V3)
- implementer-only audits (V9.5 deviation A3)
- frozen validators without negative fixtures (V9.5)
- reviews claiming reruns with no receipts (iteration 8)
- mock-only QA in sandboxes without the backend (V86/V87)
- auditors making their own errors (A11 v2 audit timing direction)

The two-sided loop (design → audit → response → re-review) caught some auditor errors (A11 v2.1 review C1–C5).

Decision making. Agents propose, audit and recommend. Mr. Zhou sets scope and preferences:
- 22 Sep owner decisions in BYTE_CORE_1: byte-level, 'not blind memorization', V50/FULL_151 milestones
- a correction to the A2 control design ('this follows Mr. Zhou's correction')
- 21 Sep: avoid 1,500+ trajectory experiments, yet prefer large samples
- 25 Sep: smaller one-hour questions
- later user adoptions (COV-SUPPORT)

Many decision rules were fixed in advance and honored even when unfavorable: V19 'stop this consolidation branch'; V43 refused to relax Q0; A2 preregistered a falsifiable prediction for b_slow and rejected it; FEAS NO_CANDIDATE_SELECTED; BKR frozen selection rule; FB1 follow-up launch gate stopped on storage rather than deleting evidence; FE1 NO_DEMONSTRATED_INCREMENT; R2/Z1 corrections never overwrote old receipts.

The exceptions are post-outcome reframings: V39/V40, V88 gate removal, the CORE_RECOVERY re-tally, the stage-exit retraction of a post-hoc hard gate, and the 0.02 weight. Several of these were not routed back to the owner. FEAS v4+ introduced an explicit 'goes to the owner' (AWAITING_OWNER) status for non-clean outcomes, which is the right pattern.

Good practices worth turning into skills:
- iteration 15's amendment text: 'The 0.01-Hz floor is a new declared mechanism-screen threshold, not a correction of an unrealistic V69 rule. V69's original result remains failed' (designs/9bc7890b63c8afb9_PROTOCOL.md)
- iteration 7 explicitly 'retained the declared population after seeing the outcomes' and recorded the scope audit
- the CORE_RECOVERY re-analysis first reproduced the original analysis to 1e-16 before computing anything new
- dual independent implementations (BYTE_LEARNER v8 refined reproduced ChatGPT's run exactly; V26/V27/V39 ran by two agents)
- 'POST HOC' labeling of the BYTE_CORE_1 erratum

The lesson-loss mechanism is visible before Full151. Corrections lived in the file where they were found (A2 metrics fix; V52 interface verdict; the encode-once note; BYTE_READ_ORDER losses), not in a standing ledger imported by the next design. The ledgers that did exist (the 50+ mechanism summary, the mechanism catalog) themselves dropped verdicts until a catalog audit forced errata (28 Sep).

Chronology caveats. CATALOG era labels are conservative: the minifly iteration line, V50–V88 and A11 items are LEGACY_CHRONOLOGY_NOT_CERTIFIED or TRANSITION. Dates here come from in-document dates. The 'V88–V9.7 objective drift audit' cited by the contract and the retrospective (26 Sep) is not in this archive or the repo. Mirrored copies exist under several roots (second_try vs second_try_copy; DIGITALBABY_CLAUDE_B_* copies cited by the retrospective).

Earliest occurrence by failure class (pre-Full151), with later recurrences:
- generator or task shortcut: V26, 7 Sep; recurs 22–23 Sep and 26 Sep
- lenient NI or absence-of-harm: V27, 7 Sep; recurs 16, 21, 23 and 28 Sep, and post-Full151
- post-hoc gate repair or reinterpretation: V39/V40, 9 Sep; recurs 16, 18 and 28 Sep
- fail-open gate: V43, ~10–11 Sep; recurs 21, 22 and 26 Sep, and Oct 11
- over-scoped verdict label or cross-system attribution: V50, 11 Sep; recurs 28 Sep and October
- tautological gate: V52, 12 Sep; recurs 19–22 Sep and Oct 13–15
- fit target mismatch: physiology audit, 13 Sep
- unverifiable claimed rerun or units error: iteration 8, 13 Sep; recurs 15–16 and 29 Sep
- objective re-scope removing a failing guard: V88, 16 Sep; recurs 18 and 21–26 Sep, and October
- event-semantics scoring defect: A2, 19 Sep; recurs twice by 21 Sep
- silent empty set: A2, 19 Sep; recurs 21 and 25 Sep
- selective endpoint display: A2 timecourse, 19 Sep
- interface limit rediscovered: A2, 19 Sep; then 21 Sep ×3 and 28 Sep
- leak inflating a published milestone: BYTE_CORE_1, 22 Sep
- ignoring a prior verdict: V52→BYTE_CORE_1, 22 Sep; BYTE_READ_ORDER→BYTE_ARITH, 26 Sep
- nonfunctional causal control in science: three-mechanism, 28 Sep
- fixture/science label confusion: V88, 16 Sep; FB1, 21 Sep

skill_recommendations.name: control-liveness-gate
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any science run, every causal control branch (no-write, N_old_rel, shuffle, yoked dose) must pass a liveness fixture. On a planted case where the control matters, it must produce a different outcome from W, and its write ledger must show zero writes in exactly its named domain and nonzero elsewhere. The auditor builds the expected branch matrix literally and must not import runner helpers. Any zero-width interval or identical W/N vectors on a primary causal contrast trigger INTEGRITY_ALARM and stop interpretation.
skill_recommendations.rationale: A 'rel' vs 'relation' string mismatch voided all E3 contrasts in the three-mechanism round and Package B V2, and hid a +38 pp native E3 effect (F01). Bank-shuffle no-op controls and literal-True qualification flags (F04, F18) are the same class.

skill_recommendations.name: tri-state-gates-with-negative-fixtures
skill_recommendations.rule: Implement every gate, validator and decision function with outputs PASS, FAIL and NOT_EVALUABLE. Missing, NaN, out-of-range or zero-support inputs map to NOT_EVALUABLE and never advance. Each check ships with at least one broken variant it must reject; the rejection receipt is archived with the source lock. Zero empirical variance yields UNRESOLVED unless an exact invariant is proven.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Fail-open gates recurred four times in two weeks: V43 Q7, FULL v3 None/NaN, BYTE_CORE_1 Q7 literal True, and the V9.5 validator accepting choice 2.0 and NaN (F04, F05). They were found only by separate reviewers.

skill_recommendations.name: shared-event-semantics-library
skill_recommendations.rule: Truth, exposure, population and timing semantics (delivered vs committed truth, information onset, probe populations) must come from one versioned, tested module. New analysis scripts may not re-derive them. The module's regression fixtures must include cases where commit ≠ onset and where population width collides, and the fixtures must produce different scores.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The change_truth commit-vs-onset defect was reintroduced in new files three times within days (A2 metrics, selectivity v1, BKR V5). A coincidental anchor match hid it (F02, F03).

skill_recommendations.name: guard-removal-requires-owner-and-fresh-confirmation
skill_recommendations.rule: Any post-outcome removal, demotion, re-weighting or reinterpretation of a preregistered gate or endpoint, including reclassifying a guard as 'not a primary objective', must: (1) be written as an amendment with the original verdict kept as headline; (2) receive explicit owner approval recorded in the project log; (3) be tested on fresh worlds in a new namespace, where the removed guard's harm is a co-primary protection endpoint. The same applies to reinterpreting a peer agent's failed gate.
skill_recommendations.rationale: V88 removed the collateral-retention gate that alone rejected a candidate. The CORE_RECOVERY re-analysis deleted 12 blanket old-memory gates to reopen CONTRACT_0.05, which later showed confirmed first-return and 7-day losses. V40 softened a peer's NOT ESTABLISHED (F07, F08, F09). This was the earliest drift away from 'OLD knowledge protected'.

skill_recommendations.name: objective-and-countermodel-preflight
skill_recommendations.rule: Before freezing, a design states its E0–E4 level and runs a fixed countermodel battery against its primary gate: exact-key table, canonicalized-key table, answer-frequency or mode, symmetry, a one-bit-per-symbol class rule, and a cross-record or leak probe (first-presentation AUC at chance; a consequence-decoupled run). If any countermodel passes, the claim is downgraded or the gate redesigned. Gates on multi-part tasks use joint per-unit floors. Any set consulted for a design decision is reclassified as development.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The owner's 'not blind memorization' goal was instrumented as an E1 task an exact-key table could pass (F10). A countermodel passed BYTE_ARITH's gate, marginal gates passed half-competent lives, and a cross-record leak inflated V50-REF F1 η (F12, F13).

skill_recommendations.name: harm-semantics-and-ni-margins
skill_recommendations.rule: Protection endpoints use three-way status (POS/NEG/UNRESOLVED). Promotion needs a justified non-inferiority margin, expressed relative to the baseline effect and the owner's tolerance, plus a count of units or worlds that lost. 'No confirmed harm', 'CI includes chance' or 'not confirmed' must never become 'safe', 'absent' or 'no transfer'. Labels must be derivable from the status vector by a tested function.
skill_recommendations.rationale: A −5 pp margin hid a −2.2 pp loss (V27). Non-inferiority passed with 42/48 histories worse (V88). A 0.02 margin equaled 40–45% of baseline η (FEAS v3). 'Not confirmed' became 'confirmed absent' (FEAS v5). The catalog wrote 'no transfer by construction' (F06).

skill_recommendations.name: capability-inheritance-ledger
skill_recommendations.rule: Every claim that a core 'has' a capability names one frozen configuration (mother learner, preserved state, write/read/feedback paths, interface, task, E-level) that passed all named tasks in the same trial. Results from different configurations are reported side by side, never added. Verdict labels encode task, interface and substrate. Before designing a new core, compare against a standing capability-baselines table (e.g. V9.9A/B, V9.10C, Z0 E3, CONTENT E1) on the same assay, or explain why that is impossible.
skill_recommendations.rationale: FUNCTIONAL_CORE_ESTABLISHED was scoped to CUE8 only. CONTENT E1 and FE0 E3 came from different systems. The retrospective's A02, A03, A06 and A07 show the merge recurring. Positive native E3 facts were lost and had to be reasserted (F15, F31).

skill_recommendations.name: carry-forward-evidence-import
skill_recommendations.rule: Each new design must import, and cite by hash: (a) HARNESS_CAPABILITIES (what the evaluator can present; cache, clock and encode-once semantics); (b) the mechanism ledger rows for every variant it touches, with prior verdicts and known liabilities; (c) the current-state pointer. Reviewers fail any design that reruns a known-failed exact variant or ignores a prior interface verdict without written justification.
skill_recommendations.rationale: V52's interface verdict was ignored by BYTE_CORE_1. BYTE_READ_ORDER losses were reused in BYTE_ARITH. The encode-once limit was rediscovered four times. V48's APL failure was nearly repeated. FE1's known retention cost was retested. Designs targeted stale state (F11, F14, F19, F20, F27).

skill_recommendations.name: audit-independence-levels
skill_recommendations.rule: Every audit states its level: L0 re-read; L1 recompute from receipts with separate code; L2 replay with an independent implementation that does not import the runner; L3 adversarial tamper battery including self-consistent joint tampering. Promotion and E3 claims require L2 or higher. Implementer-only audits are labeled as such. A claimed rerun requires a receipt hash in the repo.
skill_recommendations.rationale: A log audit accepted a self-consistent tamper that replay rejected (Claude A V3). A shared-helper audit missed the dead control. The V9.5 validator was only implementer-audited. Iteration 8 found a review's 'rerun' unverifiable (F01, F23, F28).

skill_recommendations.name: generated-summaries-with-verdicts
skill_recommendations.rule: Summaries, catalogs, handoffs and memos are generated from DECISION.json and status vectors. Every quoted number appears with its preregistered verdict, E-level, failed gates, and post-hoc flag. The report generator prints every saved endpoint; a shortlist must list omitted endpoints by name. Fixture outputs carry evidence_class=FIXTURE in headers and filenames, and the publisher refuses them as verdicts.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The catalog dropped failed per-cue gates and mislabeled post-hoc refits. The A6 memo misquoted signs. The A2 shortlist hid P7 and P2. Fixture REPORT/FINAL_DECISION files mirror or invert real verdicts (F16, F17, F22).

skill_recommendations.name: can-it-fail-metric-check
skill_recommendations.rule: For each gate or metric, the designer writes how it could fail and ships a fixture where it fails. Algebraic identities (closures, nested monotonicity, by-construction ranks, A_WR=1, clock no-ops, idle-rest no-ops) are reported only as implementation checks. Retention probes must include a condition in which forgetting is possible.
skill_recommendations.rationale: By-construction 'findings' recurred from V52 (12 Sep) through A2, A6, A10, FB1 and BYTE_CORE_1, and into post-Full151 idle-rest no-ops (F18).

skill_recommendations.name: feasibility-before-confirmation-or-search
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any expensive confirmation or population search: run a small futility screen with a privileged positive control that must reach the gate on development data, and an attribution ablation naming which native component would earn the credit. Proxies may be measured only in the operating state. Engineering smoke results may change implementation or decoder definitions through a logged amendment, but never science thresholds.
skill_recommendations.rationale: 3,072 confirmation lives ran on a floor-level interface. A rest-state proxy vetoed FE1. An anti-tuning rule blocked a known decoder fix. A 131,072-candidate evolution could not reach gates that even supervised GRUs missed (F11, F14).

skill_recommendations.name: provenance-before-execution
skill_recommendations.rule: Commit every design (including chat-derived specs), runner source, environment lock and raw receipts sufficient for offline rescoring before science starts. Use single-writer locks. No destructive cleanup without a manifest and reviewer. Constants and costs in designs must be cited to a receipt or ledger row with a hash.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Lost V41/V42 protocols, an absent V87 runner, unavailable Muse files, the Trash cleanup, a summary-only pilot that forced re-simulation, concurrent writers, and costs taken from report-generation time (F20, F24, F25).

failure_classes.name: FC01 Inert or invalid causal controls and mechanism arms reported as results (control liveness)
failure_classes.definition: Path prefix used throughout: ARCH = /home/user/digitalbaby/PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/PRE_FULL151_DESIGNS_RESULTS_20261023. Definition: a control or mechanism arm that does not change the variable it claims to change is run, and its null or zero effect is read as science. Forms seen: a no-op no-write branch, a shuffle that only relabels, an unyoked dose, a hook that edits the wrong field. Merges readers E04, E18, T06, L05, F01.
failure_classes.earliest_instance: 6 Sep 2026, V20. Doc: all five fly arms (exact, compressed, shuffled, outcome-only, feedback-disabled) have identical headline accuracies in each of three seeds. This was caught only by the separate review ('The controller is running'): ARCH/results/67d35b7d1fa5f061_v20_results_review.md <- v20_results_review.md, line 7. Same day, V23: retrieve_hard8 and retrieve_soft8 equal 'ordinary' on every accuracy column in all seeds. Only peak_mutable_numeric_bytes differs (9344 vs 3072). Source: ARCH/results/1bca2a1bde276923_SUMMARY.csv <- elm_fly_v23_20260906_173231_28825/SUMMARY.csv. SPOT-CHECKED, holds. failure_classes.mechanical_check: Before freeze, score a fixed panel of degenerate learners against every primary gate: stop after phase A, frozen layer, exact-key table, canonical-key table, hash table, mode or frequency, one-bit class rule, scalar potential, constant answer, and a cross-record integrator. If any passes, the gate is invalid or capped at the matching E-level, and any diagnostic or nondeployable arm that beats the candidate appears in the headline. Pair every retention endpoint with a current-acquisition gate. Hash every scoring-path array (reader, projections, thresholds) and require equality across arms; fail closed if a candidate parameter touches the scoring path. Use joint per-unit floors, not marginal medians. Require first-presentation AUC at chance. Promotion requires a deployment-parity panel: an uninterrupted life with experienced delays.
failure_classes.judgment_check: Which arm, real or imagined, scores best on this endpoint without having the capability? Could the optimizer reach the evaluator? Does the confirmation assay match how the learner will be used?

failure_classes.mechanical_check: Before science, compute for each gate and guard the minimum detectable effect or expected half-width at the planned n, and floor and ceiling predictions from known constants (decay, chance). A guard that cannot detect a practically material harm is NOT_ASSESSABLE and cannot license advancement without an explicit owner override, and the promotion label prints the guard's power. Materiality thresholds must be smaller than the arm's plausible effect. Any 'oracle' or 'ideal' estimator must score at least as high as every learner evaluated on the same data. Negative claims require a positive control run on the executed code path, not the design table. Report the count of units that lost, not only the mean. Status strings come from a tested POS/NEG/UNRESOLVED function.

failure_classes.mechanical_check: Every design starts with an inherited-findings ledger. It quotes, by path and hash, every audit finding, limitation and erratum recorded against each reused artifact (code, stream, run, verdict, interface), each marked RESOLVED (with evidence), OPEN or ACCEPTED. Tooling refuses to reuse a generator, stream or result with OPEN items unless the threats section names them. failure_classes.mechanical_check: Before a design cites any prior candidate as working, default, anchor, baseline or established, it mechanically loads that candidate's decision file and quotes its status and gate count in the header. Any non-pass is auto-labelled 'failed-confirmation comparator', and capability wording is blocked. Status vocabulary runs SCREENED -> CONFIRMED (fresh, locked) -> TRANSFERRED (new-workload P0 passed); 'default' or 'validated' requires CONFIRMED. A capability claim names one frozen configuration (mother learner, preserved state, read/write/feedback paths, interface, task, E-level) that passed all named tasks in the same trial. An attribution ledger records which branch produced the scored answer, a native-route lesion, and the resource ratio against native state. Adoption strings come only from a tested decision function that prints the rule and per-condition status.
failure_classes.judgment_check: Which single frozen system demonstrated this, on which assay, at which E-level, and was it confirmed on fresh data in this domain? Is the credited component the one that produced the answer?

instances: The FB1-followup fixture with an opposite sign and an identical title is the highest-risk case for automated summarizers.
failure_classes.mechanical_check: Fixture, quick, smoke, mock and engineering outputs carry evidence_class=FIXTURE (or QUICK) in the filename, title, first line and machine header. Their scientific flags are suppressed, and publishers and summarizers refuse them, including any body that says 'not scientific results'. Verdict, limit, scope and version strings are generated from the executed configuration (nonzero gene list, bounds, generations, histories) and from the computed effect sign and interval; free-text templates are forbidden. A factor whose harmful main effect has an interval excluding zero can never be labelled 'positive'. Experiment IDs are globally unique (agent, date, slug, source hash). Catalogs group design -> run -> report -> audit -> erratum lineages by folder and date, never by regex over version tokens, and report how many lineages are split.
failure_classes.judgment_check: Could a reader or agent skimming titles, filenames or JSON fields come away with the opposite conclusion?

failure_classes.mechanical_check: Before science, a full end-to-end dry run on a technical world: every arm, then aggregation, intervals and labels, plots, report, bundle, and manifest verification. Every integrity check has a fixture that must make it fail. Assert nonzero, expected-magnitude cardinality for every exclusion set, stratum and population. Use explicit identity fields and normalize types before equality. A declared state schema drives clone, digest, serialize, restore and reset, with mutation tests for each new component. Sign and magnitude fixtures for every objective, credit rule and surrogate. Library statistics only. Single-writer lockfiles. The executed source hash must equal the design-locked hash, or a signed amendment is required. Birth states ship as hashed arrays. A native prepare-only smoke test runs on the target machine.

failure_classes.mechanical_check: Before any confirmation or search: a privileged positive control must reach the gate on development data at the planned example budget. Any absolute threshold needs a feasibility witness (a constructed passing code, or a computed ceiling) on the actual workload. Fitness repeatability must be shown across independent lives of the same genome. An attribution ablation names the native component that would earn credit. Pilot and confirmation rosters are disjoint, and pilot-chosen parameters are hypotheses. A churn bound: each revision cites the validity defect it closes, and after two revisions with no outcome-changing defect, freeze or abandon with a written value-of-information statement. A frozen champion-eligibility rule refuses confirmation of a candidate that is infeasible on development data.
failure_classes.judgment_check: What decision will this run change? Could any learner pass this gate? Is another protocol revision buying information or only adding complexity?

failure_classes.mechanical_check: Keep a claim-reproduction ledger: every number taken from a proposal, review or summary is re-derived from a named table (path, version, numerator, denominator), or tagged UNVERIFIED and barred from motivating an arm or gate. Proposals declare the latest completed version they read, and stale ones are flagged automatically. Numeric 'project scores' are stripped from inputs. QA claims carry an execution level (STATIC, MOCK, NATIVE_SMOKE, NATIVE_FULL), and a claimed rerun needs a receipt hash in the repository. Audits get one rebuttal round and their own errata. Keep the user's request, proposal content and agent refinement separate, and echo back any narrowing of the user's explicit request.
failure_classes.judgment_check: Did I recompute this number, or was I told it? Am I optimizing a score that measures nothing in the contract?

review_practices_that_changed_verdicts: Recompute or replay from receipts with code independent of the runner. This is the practice that most often flipped verdicts or withdrew claims. Examples: (1) The ChatGPT scoring audit of A2 with independent replay: revision denominators corrected, the n=64 plan voided, '+11.25 pp saved' withdrawn (ARCH/results/2019838ad1e8d5fe_A2_REPORT_TO_CHATGPT_20260919.md; 86a1793ee7e8bed9_A2_FOLLOWUP_REPORT_20260919.md). (2) The A6 recomputation from NPZ with a separate implementation: gain confirmed, mechanistic explanation withdrawn (ARCH/results/58d362442643b7ea_REPORT.md). (3) The V9.5 stand-alone reducer that does not import the learner: validator defects found and the rest interpretation corrected (ARCH/results/6a9f765adc858339_AUDIT_REPORT.md). (4) The BKR V5 annotation replay: 1,536 replays, mechanism tables replaced (ARCH/results/4cd35860ea6df529_REPORT.md).

Literal-branch auditing plus a planted-defect test. The R2/Z1 correction's auditor built the branch/domain matrix literally, not from the runner helper, and had to reject a deliberately restored V2 ledger. It invalidated the three-mechanism E3 contrasts and Package B V2 receipts and revealed Z0 W-N +38.0 pp (ARCH/designs/3d468db9fadb30c3_DESIGN.md; ARCH/results/994af59f25e9acb0_REPORT.md; minifly_v3_dev_20261020/upstream/native_package/SHARED_PROTOCOL.md).

Replay audit with a self-consistent tamper battery. In Claude A V3 a jointly consistent tamper was 'accepted by the log audit and rejected by the replay', and Z2_rand was found unyoked (+5.07%) (minifly_a_v3/TECHNICAL_REPORT.md <- CLAUDE_A_V3_LAUNCH_REVIEW_20260930/). Implication: log-consistency audits are insufficient.

Cross-agent source audit before results are interpreted. Codex's V26 source audit (shift-stream contamination, new-latent probes, a gate that excludes the temporal arm by name) reframed Claude's V26 verdicts (ARCH/designs/16589886a21035e0_v26_representation_memory_design.md §3). Its later loss is an inheritance failure (FC12), not a failure of the audit.

Hostile pre-run audits that build explicit countermodels and compute small score matrices. These stopped or reshaped programs before compute was spent. BYTE_ARITH: a lookup/mode countermodel at +11.2 pp passed the gate; marginal-vs-joint gates; a decorative answer stream; leading to a program NO-GO (ARCH/results/74048eac0eaf2158_REPORT.md, d839dc4c3e33f97c_REPORT.md, 26c74d446d907733_REPORT.md). The FB1 v2/v3.1 audits recomputed windows, SDs and power (about 5,696 worlds per panel), found that confirmed harm could still advance, and caught an algebra error (ARCH/results/07e62861f41ae86c_REPORT.md, 88f0636e55be8429_REPORT.md, cb4e07086ce027e9_REPORT.md).
Independent code review before source freeze. It found V43's fail-open Q7 and the incomplete firewall coverage count before data (ARCH/results/0ac03149e9744d39_reporting_independent_review.md).

Same-agent reanalysis that first reproduces the original analysis exactly. The CORE_RECOVERY re-analysis reproduced published endpoints to 9.7e-17 before computing anything new, which made its findings credible: the ranking reversal on the true revision curve, and the regex-reconstructed ledger (ARCH/designs/96139609b9387383 line 56). The same document then removed gates post hoc (FC03), so reproduction is necessary but not sufficient.

Mandatory realized-quantity checks with locked tolerances. V69's 1% realized-dose check failed and was not relaxed, which led to exact yoking in V70 (ARCH/results/52e65c8effbb4910_REPORT.md; db74c0e7a1d51cd4_REPORT.md).

Adding a deployment-like assay as a secondary panel. V83's uninterrupted-life panel exposed the gap between branched-clone champions and REF (ARCH/results/fcae174513fd8081_REPORT.md). V86 and later moved to continuous lives.

Prespecified fresh-world confirmation gates. Step 2 on 128 fresh worlds refuted the Step 1 pilot choice (ARCH/results/d2df197c105b245c_REPORT.md). V35 C0 replication refuted 'validated' covariance (ARCH/results/5cddb9746ab60b7d_SUMMARY.md). V31's P0 adequacy gate voided mechanism verdicts on a code with no task information.

Source-to-reference reconciliation and causal prefix tests on the physiological reference. These found the future-schedule leak, 12 of 60 fit observations mismatched with the published data, and parameters at their bounds or initial values (ARCH/results/ea94e0b83866bd66_REPORT.md; fe1bf4999541ade5_REPORT.md; b02365fef53a89e3_REPORT.md).

Analytic countermodel ceilings computed inside the reports themselves: one-bit class rule, scalar potential, a cyclic family that a scalar cannot solve. These kept native E3 claims correctly narrow (V9.9B, V9.10C/D; ARCH/results/cfe49b4f76eb5442_REPORT.md, 7237c8e92dc9bcb8_REPORT.md).

Erratum before science, and POST HOC labelling. V43 PROTOCOL_ERRATUM corrected a false review sentence before execution (ARCH/designs/19b8d99740d084b4_PROTOCOL_ERRATUM.md). The BYTE_CORE_1 erratum is labelled 'POST HOC (analysis choices made after the confirmation results were seen)' (ARCH/results/39b82f8edd724356_ERRATUM_SUMMARY.json).

Implementer-only audit. V9.5 refinement audit A3: 'The implementer (Claude) is the only reviewer available... labelled implementer-audited' (ARCH/designs/c3a5d145fa3fab4f_REFINEMENT_AUDIT.md; SPOT-CHECKED). The frozen validator then accepted impossible values until a separate reducer was written.

Self-adjudicated post-hoc corrections. The V39 G2 'gate bug' fix was made, classified and accepted by the same agent, with no erratum file and identical index titles. The same document softened a peer's failed gates (FC03).

Hostile design audits whose findings were not turned into regression tests or carried-forward ledgers. The zero-variance rule (21 Sep) was lost by 28 Sep. FB1's fixed window was rewritten wrong. Encode-once was rediscovered at least four times (FC12).
Hostile test suites that verify implementation against design but cannot detect a drifted design. V88's hostile checklist enforced 'No collateral gate exists' (FC04).

Mock-only QA in sandboxes without the native backend (V86/V87), and syntax-only shipping (the V83 runner). Late crashes on unexercised paths followed (ARCH/results/f68dc82100ba1229_QA_REPORT.md; dae5ad5ccd23e3d7_V83_BACKTEST_REPORT.md).

Reviews that claimed reruns with no receipts (iteration 8). Audits with their own errors: the A11 v2 cost premise and timing direction; FB1 v2 arithmetic. The two-sided rebuttal loop caught them, but only when it was run.
Validation by matching a historical anchor that could not exercise the edge case (the A2 anchor 'passed by coincidence'), and an observer that picked the probe population by array width (FC08).

Value-of-information blindness in iterative review. FEAS went through seven same-day versions to NO_CANDIDATE_SELECTED, and A11 v3.8 was never run (FC18). Review judged validity well but cost and expected information poorly.

Era-partitioned review, including this workflow. The CATALOG era labels split design, run, report, audit and erratum chains (V9.5, V9.6, three-mechanism, R2/Z1; SPOT-CHECKED). Readers 1 and 2 each had to pull about 30-63 out-of-era documents to see corrections. A partition by catalog era alone would see invalid contrasts without their correction.
